papers_seen.author: Morrow
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach that reliably produces compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller student models. KD supports a range of transfer signals and training protocols and routinely reduces latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance in many settings. However, KD is context dependent: its success hinges on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and mitigation of failure modes. As a result, KD should be treated as the central, configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone, sufficient solution.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central and practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. A rich family of techniques — soft-target/logit distillation, feature and attention matching, projector and layer-mapping strategies, multi-teacher and teacher-free variants, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and privacy-aware formulations — enable large efficiency gains while trading off fidelity, robustness, and generalization in task- and data-dependent ways. Best practice is to treat KD as a toolbox: select what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which auxiliary methods (augmentation, selective sampling, privacy mechanisms) to combine for a given deployment constraint.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core with Clear Limits — Guidance for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely useful set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher's capability. KD spans logits transfer, intermediate feature mimicking, relational and attention-based objectives, self-distillation, ensemble-to-single transfer, and cross-modal variants. Applied thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which samples or layers to prioritize — KD can produce substantial gains in latency, memory, and sometimes robustness, but it is not a universal remedy: dataset mismatch, optimization difficulty, and propagation of teacher errors are real constraints. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a principled toolbox rather than a single recipe, summarizes practical patterns that succeed across tasks, highlights empirical failure modes, and gives evidence-backed recommendations for practitioners in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes empirical findings, methodological variants, use-cases, limitations, and practical recommendations for knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques in deep learning and NLP. Drawing solely on the provided studies, it highlights common transfer targets and training regimes, domain- and task-specific adaptations, and recurring failure modes, and offers guidance on when and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Default First‑Line, Task‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact student models from larger teachers. When matched to student capacity, teacher quality, and the available data, and when combined with complementary compression techniques, KD routinely enables favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs for deep learning and NLP. However, KD is not a universal cure: reliable deployment requires task-aware design, explicit mitigation of failure modes (capacity mismatch, transferred biases, distribution shift, and poor long‑tail behavior), and integration into an end-to-end compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, architecture choices, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Carson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods are diverse—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free protocols—and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression tools and deployment-aware data and optimization strategies. Empirical work shows KD routinely delivers substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but important limitations remain around teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, privacy, and reliable preservation of rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When adapted to task, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD preserves much of a teacher's performance while enabling lower latency, smaller memory footprint, and improved adaptability across domains and modalities. However, KD is a family of techniques rather than a single algorithm: best outcomes arise from combining distillation with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, architecture search, curriculum design, data synthesis) and from explicitly addressing challenges such as imperfect teachers, domain shift, privacy, and heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for transferring information from larger or more expensive models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models. Methods span from classic logit-based distillation to feature- and representation-level matching, adversarial and projector-based strategies, module-replacement and pruning approaches, and specialized protocols for cross-modal, federated, data-free, and generative settings. Applications range across NLP (BERT compression, machine translation, non-autoregressive models), speech and paralinguistic embeddings, vision (image translation, novel-view synthesis), 3D detection, recommender systems, and graph neural networks. Research highlights include analyses that explain why distillation works, techniques that mitigate transfer of teacher errors, curricula and selection mechanisms for better sample usage, and approaches that adapt distillation to privacy- or resource-constrained environments. Together, these works map an ecosystem of practical techniques and open challenges for deploying compact, high-performing models in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized models by transferring information from larger or alternative teachers into compact students. KD variants—ranging from logits and feature matching to relational, contrastive, and data-free protocols—have been demonstrated across vision, speech, and NLP to deliver favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. At the same time, KD’s success depends on teacher quality, signal choice, data regime, and careful training design, and it is most reliable when integrated with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware engineering. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, configurable element of any compression pipeline, but not as a standalone solution: use KD deliberately, combine it with other methods, and adopt practices that mitigate its failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable framework for producing compact models from larger teachers. When designed and deployed with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and complementary compression primitives, KD routinely yields substantial gains in efficiency with limited loss in task performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on task- and deployment‑aware choices, and important open problems remain in robustness, fairness, data‑free and privacy‑constrained settings, and principled theory linking distilled signals to student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Moss
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Aware Core for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible set of tools for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When designed around task goals, teacher–student alignment, and data availability, KD routinely enables large reductions in parameters, latency, and memory while preserving most of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher quality, student capacity, and data regimes, and it must be integrated with complementary compression primitives and explicit safeguards to meet robustness, fairness, privacy, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hughes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and deployment-ready models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. Across soft-target matching, internal-representation alignment, attention and relational signals, and data-synthesis strategies, KD is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical studies show KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance, but its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and selection, and task-aware objective design; persistent challenges include preserving low-frequency behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, handling heterogeneous architectures and non-iid data, and building principled theory that predicts when specific distillation signals will help.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Context-Dependent Tools for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression provide a practical, widely applicable route to produce smaller, faster, and often more robust models from larger teachers across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. When combined with representation-matching, contrastive objectives, multi-teacher schemes, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success depends on teacher quality, the data used for distillation, careful choice of what is transferred, and attention to fairness and domain-shift risks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as an essential yet context-sensitive component of model deployment pipelines, and summarizes best-practice recommendations and promising directions to make distillation reliably effective in applied settings.

papers_seen.author: Strong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesized Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal information. A broad toolbox of distillation targets and protocols has emerged—soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free sample synthesis, self- and online-distillation, and multi-teacher schemes—and these are routinely combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD has been applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, generative models, and federated settings, yielding large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance when design choices are task- and architecture-aware. Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and instability in optimization; practical remedies emphasize task-aware signal selection, learned teacher adaptation, layer mapping strategies, and data-synthesis or privacy-preserving protocols. This review synthesizes empirical patterns, common mechanisms, practical recommendations, and open problems for KD-driven compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable, but Insufficient Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective and practical approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Treated as a configurable toolkit—selecting what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to combine distillation with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies—KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and mitigation of bias, distribution shift, and low-frequency or rare-case behaviors. Best practice treats KD as the central component of an integrated compression pipeline tailored to task, data regime, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Challenges, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation comprises a broad set of techniques that transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) models to enable deployment under constraints of compute, memory, latency, and privacy. Over the past decade researchers have extended simple logit-matching to feature-, relation-, and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates that distilled students frequently recover a large fraction of teacher performance across vision, language, recommendation, and other modalities, but success depends on student capacity, alignment of targets and layers, the nature and availability of distillation data, and mitigation of transferred biases or teacher errors. Ongoing priorities are principled objectives for what to transfer, robust and private distillation under heterogeneous and federated data, and automated teacher–student design for practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller, deployable students. A broad toolkit of transfer targets and training protocols has been developed and routinely combined with complementary compression methods to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when applied with task‑aware choices about what to transfer, how to train, and how to integrate with pruning, quantization, and architecture design; its reliability is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Marks
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A wide set of distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive structure), training paradigms (offline, online/mutual, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation), and data strategies (real, synthetic, or data‑free) have been developed. KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and parameter count, but reliable success depends on deliberate, task‑aware choices about transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of bias, robustness, and distributional risks.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context‑Dependent Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of larger teachers' performance. KD should be treated as a first‑order component of compression pipelines, but it is not sufficient on its own: reliable deployment requires task‑aware objective selection, attention to teacher–student compatibility and data regimes, and combination with complementary compression and privacy techniques.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression strategies form a broad, practically driven toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. Across modalities and tasks—classification, generation, retrieval, graph learning, self-supervision, and reinforcement learning—research has developed many algorithmic variants (logit and feature matching, attention/relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes), system-level protocols (federated, black-box, data-free), and architecture-aware methods (task-adaptive compression, neural architecture search, pruning and quantization combinations). Empirically, KD often substantially reduces latency and parameter counts while preserving a large fraction of teacher performance, but its success depends on teacher–student alignment, available data and augmentations, and task-specific design; remaining challenges include teacher bias transfer, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, and heterogeneous-device constraints. Practical deployments balance distilled signals, data strategies, and architecture choices to achieve required trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, privacy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Weber
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD methods span soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocols such as offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, and data‑free or privacy-aware variants. Distillation is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies; its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and loss of rare behaviors. Remaining research directions include principled theory linking distillation objectives to generalization, reliable distillation under data scarcity and heterogeneous architectures, and methods that preserve robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, efficient student models. Over the past decade KD variants—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to representation-level matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or privacy-aware protocols—have been adapted to many tasks and modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal, generative models, and federated settings). Empirical work shows KD frequently preserves most teacher performance while enabling large reductions in latency, memory, and parameter count; success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data availability, and optimization. Remaining challenges include principled theory for when and what to transfer, reliable distillation across heterogeneous architectures and non‑i.i.d. data, mitigation of bias and teacher errors, and robust data-free or privacy-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones. It supports multiple information-transfer mechanisms (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and can be adapted to constrained settings (limited data, privacy, heterogeneous devices). KD is most effective when used as part of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or pretraining—and when practitioners mitigate known failure modes such as bias transfer, rare-token degradation, or teacher–student mismatch. With careful design choices (what to transfer, how to align layers, which data to use), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while largely preserving task performance across modalities.

papers_seen.author: Strong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesized Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal information. A broad toolbox of distillation targets and protocols has emerged—soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free sample synthesis, self- and online-distillation, and multi-teacher schemes—and these are routinely combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD has been applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, generative models, and federated settings, yielding large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance when design choices are task- and architecture-aware. Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and instability in optimization; practical remedies emphasize task-aware signal selection, learned teacher adaptation, layer mapping strategies, and data-synthesis or privacy-preserving protocols. This review synthesizes empirical patterns, common mechanisms, practical recommendations, and open problems for KD-driven compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Tool for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable, task-aware component of a broader compression pipeline, KD can deliver substantial gains in latency, memory, and often accuracy while enabling deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, signal selection, and complementary compression methods. Responsible application requires explicit mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and bias transfer, and integration with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, or data‑free methods when appropriate.

Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD can preserve a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but its effectiveness is context dependent: success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthesis, and safeguards against propagated biases, privacy leakage, and degraded behavior on low-frequency or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for producing compact, deployable models from larger teacher models. papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for transferring predictive behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. KD spans logits-based supervision, feature and relational matching, adversarial or synthetic data generation, and architectural or curriculum adaptations. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, and complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD can enable deployment in latency- and resource-constrained settings and sometimes yield students that match or exceed teacher performance, but it also carries risks—propagating teacher errors and biases, struggling under data scarcity or mismatch, and requiring task-specific engineering. I argue KD should be treated as a central component of compression pipelines, applied conditionally with targeted remedies and validated against task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are now core tools for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance and functionality of larger teachers. The literature has expanded far beyond simple logits matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, many-to-many layer mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, multi-teacher and teacher-engineering strategies, and tight integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from teacher to student. A broad family of distillation techniques has been developed—logit (soft-label) matching, feature and layer-wise mimicry, multi-teacher and confidence-weighted schemes, adversarial and contrastive objectives, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—enabling deployment across vision, language, graphs, recommender systems, and federated settings. While distillation often preserves most teacher performance and can even improve student generalization, effectiveness depends on what is transferred, layer alignment, teacher quality, availability and match of data, and complementary compression methods. This synthesis summarizes the operational variants, key empirical findings, domain-specific applications, common failure modes, and practical recommendations distilled from the provided studies.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential, empirically validated approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD methods—ranging from soft‑logit matching to intermediate‑feature and attention transfers, adversarial or contrastive objectives, and multi‑teacher schemes—regularly enable large reductions in inference cost and parameter footprint while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD’s effectiveness is strongly dependent on the distillation objective, teacher–student alignment, data availability and quality, and optimization dynamics; therefore, reliable compression in practice requires combining KD with task‑aware design choices and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis) and explicit mitigation strategies for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller, more efficient student models. KD reduces inference cost, memory footprint, and communication overhead while often preserving much of the teacher’s performance across vision, language, speech, generation, and multimodal tasks. Its practical value arises when KD is designed around task objectives, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints, and when it is combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of techniques has emerged — from soft-label/logit transfer to feature- and layer-level matching, adversarial or ensemble-driven schemes, data-free generation, and task-adaptive architecture search — yielding practical gains across NLP, vision, speech, and recommendation systems. Successes are widespread, but effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful alignment of objectives; combining KD with complementary compression methods and task-aware design is generally required for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of methods that transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD can materially reduce latency, memory, and energy costs while preserving much of teacher performance, and its variants (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational objectives, online/mutual schemes, and data-free synthesis) extend its applicability across tasks and deployment constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and the choice of which signals to transfer; practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware practices rather than as a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Applications (Synthesis)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A broad toolkit has emerged — including logits/soft-label transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, online and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search — enabling deployment across vision, speech, language, generative, and multimodal settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights gains in latency, memory, calibration, and sometimes robustness, while pointing to failure modes driven by teacher quality, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and distribution shift; best practice treats KD as a core element of a broader, context-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Central, Practical, and Responsible Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable set of techniques that enables compact models to inherit much of the performance and functionality of larger teachers. When combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and tailored to task and data constraints, KD unlocks deployment on latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained platforms while supporting modalities from language to vision and multimodal systems. However, KD is not automatic: careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, rare-token degradation) are required for responsible, robust outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Settings, and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies are now widespread across computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation systems, and specialized settings (federated, few-shot, multi-modal, generative). Research has advanced along multiple axes: what to transfer (logits, features, attention, latent modules), how to shape the transfer (sample selection, adversarially-informed examples, curriculum, teacher ensembles, meta-learning), and special protocols for constrained environments (federated/black-box, few-shot, on-device inference). Empirical work shows KD can substantially close the performance gap between small and large models, enable practical deployment of generative and discriminative models, and, when extended, transfer robustness and interpretability. Remaining challenges include error propagation from teachers (especially for low-frequency phenomena), limitations under data heterogeneity in federated settings, and task-specific design choices for complex outputs (e.g., detection, segmentation, set outputs), motivating continued work on tailored distillation objectives and teacher-student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Watts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Aware, and Integrative Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical and conceptual work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and inductive biases to produce substantial gains in latency, memory, and often accuracy. However, KD has concrete failure modes—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, propagation of teacher artifacts, and distribution shift—that limit its effectiveness when used alone. The most reliable outcomes arise when KD is treated as a configurable core of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that combines careful teacher engineering, targeted distillation signals, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teachers to smaller students. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with task‑aware objectives and complementary compression techniques, but it must be integrated with targeted data, architectural, and fairness-aware practices to address limitations such as distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, low-frequency behavior loss, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Dalton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach that reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD works via multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, adversarial, data‑free). Its practical value comes from being a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies—rather than a single, automatic cure‑all. Realizing KD's benefits requires careful choices about teacher selection, student capacity and architecture, distilled signals, training data, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of approaches for transferring information from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, efficient student models to reduce computation, memory, latency, and communication while attempting to preserve task performance. Over the past decade these techniques have expanded from simple soft-target (logit) supervision to a broad, configurable toolkit that includes intermediate representation matching, attention and relational objectives, online and self-distillation, data‑free and adversarial synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling practical deployment on constrained hardware, but outcomes depend critically on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and design of data for distillation, and mitigation strategies for transferred errors, distribution shift, and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under constraints of compute, memory, latency, and privacy. The literature develops a broad taxonomy of distillation signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational maps, contrastive objectives), training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, self-distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free and federated), and integrations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows distilled students can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while greatly improving efficiency, but success is context-dependent, hinging on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of bias, robustness, and privacy risks. Best practice treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component within integrated compression pipelines rather than a standalone recipe, and open problems remain in principled choice of distilled targets, reliable distillation with limited or private data, and theory connecting distilled signals to student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Wallace
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A rich family of distillation targets and protocols has been developed (from soft logits to feature- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants), and KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods and task-aware data and architecture strategies. Success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and augmentation, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as transferred bias, capacity mismatch, and degraded behavior on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of the Provided Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact student models. The literature frames KD as a configurable toolkit that includes matching teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- and relational-level transfer, adversarial or data‑free synthesis of training signals, and diverse protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, federated). KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical studies show distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance across vision, language, and other modalities, but effectiveness depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as transferred biases, distribution shift, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a central, task‑aware component of integrated compression pipelines rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all cure.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Cunningham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used family of techniques for transferring behavior from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—including logits/soft-target matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and adversarial generation, and self-distillation—are combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines typically recover most teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of transfer signals, and the availability or synthesis of data; remaining challenges include robustness, bias transfer, low-frequency/structured-output preservation, privacy-aware distillation, and automating teacher–student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Domains, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger or multi-source models to smaller, faster, or modality-restricted models to reduce memory, compute, and latency while retaining performance. Approaches vary from matching teacher logits to mimicking internal features, and extend to self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and adaptations for few-shot, federated, and multimodal settings. Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative models shows KD can enable compact models that approach teacher accuracy, improve calibration and fairness, and make deployment on resource-constrained and heterogeneous devices practical. Ongoing challenges include selecting what to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning heterogeneous architectures, and designing KD protocols robust to limited data, domain shifts, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broadly applicable toolkit for producing smaller, faster, or more interpretable models from large teacher networks. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representation matching, attention/relational signals, and synthetic data, and they commonly combine KD with pruning, quantization, and automated architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most teacher performance while substantially reducing latency and memory, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and task-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Sampson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Tool for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, widely applicable approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller, efficient students. KD routinely yields substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or deployment-ready compression: its success depends on choices of distilled signals, data and augmentation strategies, teacher–student alignment, and combination with complementary compression techniques. Treating KD as the core of a task-aware, integrated compression pipeline — rather than a one-shot solution — achieves the best tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, evidence-backed approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable models across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD methods — ranging from logits transfer to intermediate-feature matching, self-distillation, and selective-sample protocols — routinely enable substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: success depends on what information is transferred, teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data choices, and integration with complementary compression techniques. When treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline, KD provides a practical route to deploy high-performing models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Research and practice have developed a diverse toolkit — matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features and attention, using contrastive/relational objectives, generating or selecting distillation data, multi-teacher and online schemes, and combining KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, speech, and multimodal tasks shows distilled students frequently recover much of teacher performance, though effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and alignment of objectives and representations. Key open problems include reliable transfer of rare or structured behaviors, robust distillation under data heterogeneity and privacy constraints, principled teacher selection and co-design, and automated, task-aware distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Fitzgerald
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practical family of methods for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD transfers information at multiple levels—from soft logits to intermediate features, attention maps, relational and contrastive structures—and is implemented in diverse protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co‑distillation, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants). In practice KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when its design is matched to teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. Important limitations and open problems remain, including principled theory linking transferred signals to student generalization, robust distillation under distribution shift and data‑scarce or privacy‑sensitive regimes, mitigation of biased or low‑frequency behavior transfer, and automated layer/representation alignment strategies.

papers_seen.author: Bolton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Configurable Core of Model‑Compression Pipelines: Necessary, Versatile, and Bounded
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile family of methods that should be treated as a configurable core within integrated model‑compression pipelines. KD routinely yields large efficiency gains across modalities but is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on aligning distilled signals, teacher–student capacity and architectures, data strategies (including data‑free or privacy‑aware regimes), and complementary compression primitives. Effective deployment therefore requires task‑aware choices, safeguards for robustness and fairness, and continued work on principled theory and reliable distillation under limited or heterogeneous data.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal domains, a diverse set of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi‑teacher, data‑free or self‑distillation) have been developed. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover much of a teacher’s performance while enabling lower latency, reduced memory use, and new deployment modes; success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful design of the transfer objective. Practical pipelines commonly pair KD with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task‑aware procedures (layer mapping, curriculum, teacher adaptation) to meet deployment constraints. Important open problems include robust transfer under distribution shift and data scarcity, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, principled automated design for heterogeneous student architectures, and privacy‑aware or data‑free distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical approach for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants and training protocols enable large reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Real-world success depends on task- and capacity-aware choices of distillation signals, teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including data-free and federated variants), and combination with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is powerful but conditional: it frequently yields strong trade-offs in practice but requires careful treatment of teacher quality, data regimes, and robustness or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context‑Sensitive Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD methods range from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature, attention, relational and adversarial objectives, and operate in offline, online, data‑free and federated regimes. While KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, its success is context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data strategy, and complementary compression primitives strongly determine outcomes. For reliable deployment, KD should be treated as the core of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of task performance. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, KD methods range from soft-target (logit) matching to richer objectives that mimic internal representations, attention, relational structure, or contrastive signals. KD is frequently combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapted to practical constraints via data-free, few-shot, online, or federated protocols. Success depends on careful, task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited data, privacy, distribution shift, and undesirable teacher behaviors. The literature emphasizes KD as a configurable component of broader compression pipelines rather than a turnkey algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are widely used to produce smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Work across theory, computer vision, natural language processing, graph learning and systems has explored why distillation works, how to make it practical under constraints (limited or no access to original data, privacy, federated settings), and how to adapt it to specialized settings (pretrained language models, non-autoregressive translation, detectors, GANs, visual-linguistic models). Empirical and theoretical studies identify benefits, failure modes, and design patterns: distillation often simplifies learning targets and stabilizes optimization; matching intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure can improve transfer; mixing soft and hard targets can correct teacher errors; and specialized procedures (e.g., layer mapping, adversarial sample generation, teacher adaptation) are effective for particular tasks. Remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous or private data, preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior in sequence tasks, and formalizing the optimal teacher-student pairing and data complexity trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Bowen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Component for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed and applied with awareness of task constraints, teacher quality, student capacity, and available data, KD enables large reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: it must be integrated with complementary compression methods and explicit safeguards to address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, distribution shift, and propagation of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Mann
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. The literature has expanded KD beyond simple soft-target matching to include representation- and structure-level objectives, a variety of training schedules (offline, online, self-distillation, data-free), and many task- and architecture-aware adaptations. Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves most of teacher performance and sometimes improves robustness or calibration, but outcomes are sensitive to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the data available for distillation, and the particular signals chosen for transfer. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture choices—and emphasizes task-aware design, data strategies, and safeguards against transferred biases or degraded low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, pragmatic framework for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teachers into compact students. KD methods span soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and variants for online, multi-teacher, data‑free, federated, and self‑distillation regimes. The most reliable deployments treat KD not as a single recipe but as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.
