papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. Across tasks and modalities KD methods (logit/soft‑target matching, intermediate feature or attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, online/self‑distillation, and data‑free variants) routinely improve student accuracy and efficiency when combined with task‑aware design choices and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover a substantial fraction of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data regime and alignment, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, loss of low‑frequency behavior, distribution shift, and privacy concerns. Open directions emphasize principled theory for transfer objectives, data‑efficient and privacy‑preserving protocols, heterogeneous and federated deployments, and robust evaluation under realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gomez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, latency, and communication while attempting to preserve task performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate features, attention and relational signals, contrastive and adversarial objectives) and supports a variety of training protocols and data strategies. In practice, KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline together with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and appropriate data procedures. Success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distillation targets and data, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as propagated errors, distribution shift, and fairness/privacy risks. Remaining needs include stronger theoretical links between distilled signals and generalization, reliable distillation under heterogeneous or limited data, and robust privacy- and safety-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practical approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable toolbox rather than a single algorithm, KD enables large reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance across modalities. Its effectiveness depends on task-aware choices—what signals to transfer, how to align architectures, how to generate or select transfer data, and which complementary compression techniques to combine. KD also has clear failure modes (data scarcity, teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena) that require targeted remedies. With appropriate safeguards and joint optimization with pruning, quantization, or architecture search, KD should be a primary method in compression pipelines, applied conditionally and validated for the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal representations. The field has matured from simple soft‑target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate‑feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, online and self‑distillation, multi‑teacher and data‑free protocols, and architecture‑aware adaptations. KD is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance, but its practical success is context dependent and requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and mitigation of bias, robustness, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Tool for Model Compression and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher→student logits-matching recipe into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing models and enabling deployment under constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous hardware. Modern KD variants transfer not only soft labels but also internal and feature representations, employ multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, and integrate with federated and data-constrained workflows. When matched to the task (e.g., feature-level distillation for representation-heavy NLP, projector adapters for mismatched architectures, or privacy-aware ensembles for federated settings), KD enables small models to approximate or sometimes match larger teachers while offering routes to improved robustness and inclusivity. However, realizing these gains requires attention to teacher quality, capacity gaps, the form of distilled information, and sample-wise effects of soft targets. I argue that KD should be treated as a first-order, configurable component of model-compression pipelines and present evidence-based practical recommendations for when and how to apply its variants.

papers_seen.author: Berry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Benefits, Limits, and Practical Prescriptions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring behavior or internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Empirically, KD reduces inference latency, memory footprint, and compute while often preserving most of a teacher's task performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD methods vary in what they transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), how data are used (real, augmented, synthesized, or zero-shot), and whether distillation is performed online, with multiple teachers, or self-supervised. KD is most effective when configured to task and deployment constraints and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware search). It also has well-documented failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagated teacher artifacts, degraded long-tail performance, and data-availability or privacy limits—that require explicit mitigation strategies. This synthesis summarizes established techniques, practical trade-offs, and actionable design patterns for applying KD in real-world deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, widely applicable technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models to compact students across vision, language, generative, and distributed settings. For practical, high-fidelity compression, KD should be treated as a core component of a broader pipeline that includes pre-training of compact architectures, careful layer- and feature-level alignment, multi-teacher or meta-learned teaching strategies, data-aware augmentation or synthesis, and complementary compression methods such as pruning or quantization.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, Practical Strategies, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of task performance. papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have evolved from a simple teacher-to-student logits-matching recipe into a broad toolbox for producing compact, efficient, and adaptable models in vision, speech, and natural language processing. Research has produced a range of practical methods—logit and feature matching, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data- and privacy-aware variants, and federated or online protocols—and has clarified connections to regularization, ensemble learning, and optimization. Empirical work shows KD can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher's performance, though gains depend on teacher quality, data used for distillation, and adaptation to deployment constraints. This synthesis summarizes core methods, theoretical insights, empirical findings, practical considerations, and open challenges that shape current best practice for KD-driven compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their accuracy. Empirical results across vision, language, retrieval, detection, generative models, and distributed settings show KD can close much of the performance gap between large and compact models, but best outcomes require tailoring what and how knowledge is transferred and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques and domain-aware procedures.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Woods
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, Practical Guidance, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers into compact students. KD methods operate at multiple levels—from soft-label (logit) matching to feature-, attention-, and relation-level transfers—and have been adapted to many training and deployment protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co‑distillation, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free, and federated schemes). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, retrieval, and recommendation shows that KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and distillation data are properly matched. In practice, KD is most effective when used as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that includes complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, pretraining, data augmentation, and careful layer alignment. Remaining challenges include handling teacher biases and errors, preserving low-frequency or minority behaviors, operating under data absence or strict privacy constraints, and automating teacher–student design for heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Berger
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. A wide range of distillation targets and protocols has been developed, and KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design. While distilled students often recover much of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, important limitations and open problems remain—particularly around data scarcity, distribution shift, bias transfer, and principled selection of distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large models for deployment across domains and modalities. When designed with task-awareness (choice of distilled signal, teacher selection, and training scheme), KD can preserve accuracy while materially improving latency, memory, and privacy characteristics. Best results arise from combining multiple KD techniques (logit, feature, layer-wise, adversarial, and ensemble-based) chosen to match the task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, and multimodal settings. It can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, and it interacts naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, distillation's success depends on the distillation objective, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and task-specific considerations; when these are not addressed it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with rare outputs, or fail due to optimization issues. Best practice is to treat KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines—combining logits, intermediate feature matching, projector modules, multi-teacher or teacher-adaptive designs, and data-aware schedules—to maximize student utility in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Necessity, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are essential engineering primitives for making large deep models practical in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, language, and multimodal tasks show that carefully chosen distillation targets, training schedules, and data strategies enable small students to recover much of teacher performance. At the same time, important challenges remain—data heterogeneity, teacher–student mismatch, low-frequency behavior preservation, and principled teacher selection—motivating focused research and deployment practices.

papers_seen.author: Fuller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods that transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models to reduce latency, memory, and compute while retaining much of teacher performance. KD spans approaches that match softened outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive structures, and data-side strategies (including data-free synthesis and privacy-aware workflows). Empirical work shows KD routinely improves accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks when it is adapted to teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline that combines objective design, architecture-aware choices, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search) together with explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthetic Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—matching teacher logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployment commonly integrates KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires careful, task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. Key challenges include propagation of teacher errors, degradation on low-frequency or structured outputs, data and domain mismatch, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often multi-source or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Across vision, language, speech, multimodal and generative settings, KD has evolved beyond simple logit matching to include representation- and relation-level objectives, adversarial or data-free generation, online and self-distillation protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization and architecture search. These approaches routinely enable large reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but reliable deployment requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. Important open directions remain in principled theory, robust distillation under heterogenous and low-data regimes, and preserving long-tail or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation Is Central but Insufficient: A Case for Integrated, Context‑Aware Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations across modalities and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and careful choice of transfer signals; for robust, real-world compression KD should be treated as a configurable component of integrated pipelines that include complementary compression primitives and explicit safeguards for bias, robustness, and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Becker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for training smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods transfer predictive signals (soft logits), representational signals (intermediate features, attention maps), and relational or contrastive knowledge. KD is routinely combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and data-side strategies (sample selection, synthetic-data generation, curriculum design). Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve deployability, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, choice of distillation signals, and data availability; common failure modes include transferred biases, degraded rare-event/low-frequency behavior, and sensitivity to distribution shift. Practical deployment treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across domains and tasks—language modeling and translation, recommendation, graph learning, vision, continual and domain adaptation, and resource-constrained deployment—KD enables trade-offs between accuracy, latency, memory, privacy, and train-time complexity. Variants such as feature mimicking, self- and teacher-free distillation, ensemble and online distillation, data-free and privacy-aware schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations extend KD’s applicability. At the same time, careful choice of training targets, treatment of low-frequency phenomena, and consideration of the teacher-student mismatch are necessary to avoid transferring teacher errors and to realize the full benefits of distillation.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, graph, generative, and multimodal domains, KD methods range from soft‑target (logit) matching to richer objectives that align intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure, or contrastive signals. KD is most effective when embedded in integrated compression pipelines that also leverage pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and when the distillation protocol is tailored to task constraints, student capacity, and available data. Practical deployment requires addressing known failure modes—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, propagation of teacher biases or errors, and degraded performance on rare or structured outputs—and pursuing targeted remedies such as task‑aware teacher design, data synthesis or augmentation, projector layers, and joint optimization with complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or deployment-specialized student models. A rich set of transfer targets and protocols—ranging from soft-label/logit matching to feature- and attention-level alignment, relational/contrastive objectives, and data- or generator-based synthesis—has been developed and successfully applied across vision, language, speech, recommender systems, and multimodal domains. Practical KD pipelines typically combine distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and projector layers), and their success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and explicit mitigations for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining challenges include principled theory linking teacher signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under heterogeneous architectures and non-iid data, privacy-aware protocols, and preserving rare or structured behaviors under compression.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Versatile, but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports diverse transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), adapts to data-limited and privacy‑sensitive settings, and interoperates with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its empirical strengths make KD a first‑line approach for many deployment problems, but reliable, production‑grade compression requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data selection or synthesis, capacity matching, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Beltran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A broad toolbox has been developed—logit/soft‑target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, contrastive and relational objectives, online and multi-teacher protocols, and data‑free or privacy‑aware approaches—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD routinely enables substantial efficiency gains while recovering a large fraction of teacher performance, but its success is context dependent and requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data regimes, and explicit mitigations for propagated errors, bias, and distribution shift. Remaining needs include stronger theory linking objectives to student generalization, automated teacher–student alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and robust privacy- and data-scarce distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Bauer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically proven approach for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they meet latency, memory, compute, and deployment constraints. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness. While KD can recover much of teacher performance across modalities, reliable deployment requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated toolbox for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants and protocols enable substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. In practice KD is context dependent: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and explicit mitigation of transferred biases, robustness deficits, and privacy concerns. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline that combines distillation with complementary techniques—pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—rather than as a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer behavior and representations from larger, more expensive models into smaller, efficient ones while retaining task performance. Across modalities and tasks, research has developed many complementary mechanisms — soft-label mimicry, intermediate representation matching, teacher-student curriculum designs, self-distillation, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- or generator-based transfer, and domain- or modality-specific adaptations — to balance accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation can recover most teacher performance (and in some settings even surpass it) while enabling deployment on constrained hardware and improving reproducibility and privacy. Success depends on the distillation targets, the teacher-student pairing and training regime, the use of auxiliary data or synthetic examples, and task-specific modifications.

papers_seen.author: Cooper
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely used paradigm for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets and training protocols and is most effective when integrated with task-aware objectives, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression primitives. While KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the nature or availability of distillation data, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as propagated biases, distribution shift, and degraded behavior on rare or structured outputs. Practical use therefore treats KD as a configurable component of broader compression pipelines rather than a one-shot cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used family of techniques for transferring capabilities from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce latency, memory, and energy costs while preserving task performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal domains, KD has evolved beyond logits-only supervision into rich protocols that match intermediate features, attention patterns, relational or contrastive structures, and even synthesized data or generator-based replay. Practical deployments combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies; success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and careful objective and layer alignment. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical patterns, practical recommendations, and open challenges documented in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Cain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger “teacher” models to compact “student” models. Across modalities and tasks, KD has been adapted to operate on output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structures, and it can run in offline, online, multi‑teacher, or data‑free regimes. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers much of a teacher’s performance and, when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and training strategies, produces production‑ready tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity. However, KD is context‑sensitive: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, alignment of inputs and layers, data availability and distribution, and risks of transferring teacher errors or biases all shape outcomes. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline with targeted mitigations for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Necessary but Insufficient Core for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. KD methods include logit/soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-free or adversarial example synthesis. Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms; however, KD alone does not resolve challenges such as teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity and scarcity, preservation of rare-token or long-tail behavior, and the transfer of teacher biases. Effective compression pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable core component that must be combined with task-aware engineering, complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, hardware-aware design), and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. The literature shows a diverse set of distillation targets and training regimes, and repeatedly demonstrates that KD—when matched to task constraints and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies—can deliver large reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance. Success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, objective design, and explicit practices to mitigate propagated biases and robustness failures. Remaining open problems center on formalizing when specific KD signals preserve generalization, reliable distillation under scarce or private data, transfer across heterogeneous architectures, and principled mitigation of harmful transferred behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Lamb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Conditional Core of Model-Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically proven approach for producing smaller, faster, or deployment-specialized models in deep learning and NLP. When treated as a configurable core technique—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods and data strategies—KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of failure modes (bias propagation, low-frequency phenomena, and distribution shift). Robust deployment requires task-aware design, multi-signal objectives, and integration with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis strategies.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD techniques extend beyond matching logits: they include internal-representation distillation, adversarial and relational approaches, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware methods, and architecture-aware replacements. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve or even improve generalization, enable domain adaptation, and permit deployment under resource, privacy, or latency constraints—provided practitioners attend to known failure modes such as teacher bias, low-frequency lexical errors, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Efficient and Robust Deep Models: Evidence, Techniques, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher→student transfer recipe into a broad set of methods that enable model compression, robustness, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving training, and architectural search. Across modalities and tasks—NLP, speech, vision, graphs, ranking and recommender systems—KD-based approaches consistently trade minimal performance loss for large gains in speed, memory, interpretability or deployability. The diversity of KD formulations (feature-based, layer-mapping, data-free, online/mutual, multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, and task-adaptive compression) provides practitioners with targeted tools to address constraints such as limited data, non-iid federated shards, low-frequency tokens in translation, and privacy requirements. Based on empirical results across the literature, KD should be considered a first-order technique in any pipeline that must deliver high-quality models under resource, privacy, or latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hopkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. Across modalities and tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and relation-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial schemes, and data‑free generation—regularly produce large size and latency reductions with modest performance loss when designed in a task- and deployment-aware way. Practical success is conditional on teacher quality, data regime, teacher–student alignment, and safeguards against propagation of undesirable teacher properties; addressing open problems (robust data-free distillation, theory of transfer, fairness and privacy) requires integrating KD into end-to-end compression pipelines and co-designing students, objectives, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teacher models. KD methods span output-level supervision, intermediate representation matching, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-aware or data-free protocols. While KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness, its success is strongly context dependent: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data availability and synthesis, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy determine practical outcomes. As a result, KD should be treated as a configurable, first‑line element of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Mcdaniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD is effective across modalities when treated as a configurable toolbox—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relations), how to align teacher and student (layer mapping, projectors, curricula), and how to handle data constraints (augmentation, data-free synthesis, federated protocols). KD routinely recovers much of teacher performance and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, but it is context-dependent: limitations include teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias propagation, and difficulties with rare/long-tail phenomena. Best practice is to use KD as a principled component of an integrated compression pipeline, paired with task-aware design choices and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as a configurable, task-aware toolkit and combined with complementary compression methods, distillation enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. However, its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and data strategy; it must be applied conditionally with safeguards against error and bias propagation.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Configurable Core of Model Compression: Essential but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile set of techniques that transfer information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. KD variants match soft logits, internal representations, attention maps, or relational structure and support offline, online, multi-teacher, and data‑free protocols. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can enable new capabilities (e.g., cross‑task transfer, self‑supervision for small models), but practical success depends on careful engineering: choosing what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and architecture, managing data strategies, and integrating KD with complementary compression primitives. Remaining challenges include principled theory, reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy limits, mitigation of bias transfer, and effective procedures for structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Sparks
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, Task‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression (with Explicit Limits and Prescriptions)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, first‑line strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students because it is flexible, empirically effective across modalities, and interoperable with complementary compression primitives. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on task‑aware choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data regime, and explicit mitigations for transferred bias, capacity mismatch, and low‑frequency behaviors. Practitioners should adopt KD as a configurable core within integrated pipelines that include task adaptation, selective or curriculum distillation, and complementary methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture search) to meet concrete deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression: Effective but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs, but its success is strongly context dependent. Practical deployments treat KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—rather than a standalone solution. Responsible application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and targeted mitigations for bias, rare behaviours, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. When combined with pre-training, careful choice of distillation signals, data- and task-aware strategies, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture replacement), KD produces compact models that approach teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, availability or synthesis of data, alignment of internal representations, and consideration of fairness and robustness. Best practice therefore treats KD as a flexible toolkit—mixing soft-label transfer, feature- or layer-level matching, online/ensemble schemes, and domain-aware adjustments—to meet practical production requirements.

papers_seen.author: Craig
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models by transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into compact student models. Across modalities and tasks, a diverse toolbox of distillation targets and training protocols has been developed and combined with complementary compression methods to meet latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance and enable practical deployment, but success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability, and explicit measures to mitigate failure modes such as bias transfer, optimization gaps, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad family of techniques for compressing large or expensive models into smaller, faster, or more deployable ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Methods differ in the form of transferred knowledge (soft logits, hidden features, contrastive distributions, synthetic data, or cross-modal alignments), in how and when distillation is applied (offline, online, layer-wise, task-adaptive, or data-free), and in the problems they target (classification, detection, generation, language tasks, graph learning, or novel-view synthesis). Empirical work demonstrates that appropriate choices about teacher signals, data manipulation, and architectural search can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities; theoretical work begins to clarify when soft labels help and when hard labels or mixed supervision are needed. Remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, dataset and fairness concerns, and scaling distillation reliably in large distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high‑capacity teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, generative and multimodal tasks, KD has been adapted into many targets and training regimes and is most effective when integrated with architecture‑aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. This synthesis summarizes the empirical strengths of KD, the principal methods and protocols, common limitations, and practical design patterns that guide successful compression and deployment.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, empirically grounded toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners choose among soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-free or federated protocols; these methods are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on principled choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and targeted mitigations for transferred biases and distribution-shift failures.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, KD techniques (logits, feature/attention matching, relational objectives, adversarial and data‑free protocols, and ensemble/online schemes) often recover a large fraction of teacher performance when paired with appropriate data strategies, pretraining, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD has concrete limits — teacher error propagation, capacity mismatch, rare‑token degradation, and failures under distribution shift or scarce/private data — which motivate task‑aware design, multi‑signal objectives, and integration with other compression primitives. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical patterns, domain examples, practical guidelines, and open challenges documented in the selected literature.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach to compressing large models for deployment and domain-specific use. Across modalities and tasks, KD can preserve much of the teacher's performance in compact students, but it must be combined with task-aware engineering—such as teacher adaptation, layer-wise selection, data augmentation, and hardware-aware pruning—to address heterogeneity, domain shift, and efficiency constraints. This article argues that KD is necessary but not sufficient: best results come from integrating KD with complementary techniques chosen for the target modality, deployment constraints, and learning scenario.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. It enables deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints across vision, language, and multimodal tasks while supporting robustness and transfer when combined with task-aware design. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher and data quality, architectural alignment, and complementary compression techniques, and it can propagate teacher biases and fail on low-frequency or out-of-distribution phenomena unless mitigated.

papers_seen.author: Cole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient, Task‑Aware Core for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable technique for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. Empirical and methodological work across modalities shows KD frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and supports many deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). However, KD's success is conditional on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and degraded handling of low‑frequency phenomena. Best practice treats KD as a configurable, task‑aware component within an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation‑aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet real deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Ubiquitous, but Demand-Aware
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for compressing high-capacity models into efficient students across modalities and tasks. Empirical results across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and generative settings show KD can recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on how knowledge is represented and transferred (logits, features, attention, contrastive objectives), the alignment between teacher and student inputs, the data used for distillation, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Carefully chosen distillation algorithms and extensions (self-supervised distillation, meta-learned teachers, multi-teacher weighting, online and distributed schemes, and privacy-preserving perturbations) can mitigate common failure modes and broaden KD’s applicability in production and research settings.

papers_seen.author: Gibbs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible suite of methods for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students. Empirical evidence across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and federated settings shows KD can produce compact models with much of the teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD’s practical value increases when combined with complementary compression techniques and when its design is adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints; however, its reliability depends on addressing well-documented failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, and propagation of teacher artifacts. This review argues that KD should be treated as a central but context‑aware tool: essential to modern compression pipelines but most effective when paired with targeted algorithmic and engineering practices.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practical approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable toolbox rather than a single algorithm, KD enables large reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance across modalities. Its effectiveness depends on task-aware choices—what signals to transfer, how to align architectures, how to generate or select transfer data, and which complementary compression techniques to combine. KD also has clear failure modes (data scarcity, teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena) that require targeted remedies. With appropriate safeguards and joint optimization with pruning, quantization, or architecture search, KD should be a primary method in compression pipelines, applied conditionally and validated for the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of methods for transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under constraints of compute, memory, latency, or privacy. Across vision and natural language tasks, distillation targets range from soft logits to intermediate representations and relational signals; KD is frequently combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with domain- or task-specific procedures to improve efficacy. KD delivers strong empirical gains in many settings but is bounded by teacher quality, availability and match of data, teacher–student capacity gaps, and the risk of transferring teacher biases; effective application therefore requires task-aware choices of signals, data strategies, and often hybrid compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.
