papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teacher models. KD encompasses a wide array of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention and relational maps, contrastive objectives), training regimes (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free), and deployment-aware adaptations. Empirical evidence across vision, language, graph, speech, and multimodal tasks indicates KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance and yields substantial efficiency gains (reduced latency, memory, and FLOPs), but outcomes are highly context-dependent. Reliable compression typically treats KD as a configurable core component of an integrated pipeline together with pruning, quantization, architecture design/search, data strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Open problems include principled theory linking transfer signals to student generalization, better approaches for data-scarce or privacy-sensitive distillation, automated teacher–student co-design, and preserving long-tail or rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Spencer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely successful family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost, but its reliability depends on task- and data-aware design choices, teacher–student alignment, and integration with complementary compression primitives. Responsible deployment requires explicit attention to data availability, distributional shift, rare-case behaviors, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and deployment‑specialized models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Methods include matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features and attention, relational and contrastive objectives, multi‑teacher and online protocols, and data‑aware or data‑free variants. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable tool within an integrated compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias propagation, rare‑token degradation, and distribution shift. Practical deployments therefore combine careful selection of transfer targets, layer and projector design, curricula and data synthesis, and complementary compression primitives while monitoring robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and transfers information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. A wide family of distillation objectives and workflows—ranging from soft-logit matching to representation, relational, contrastive, adversarial, online, and meta-learned schemes—has been developed and applied across domains including vision, speech, graph learning, machine translation, and NLP. Empirical results show distillation often preserves most teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on careful design choices around teacher quality, student capacity, data, and objectives.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Toolkit for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger teachers to smaller students, but its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to train, and how to integrate complementary compression methods. When designed as part of a task-aware pipeline—with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and privacy or fairness constraints—KD yields deployable models that retain much of teacher performance; treated naively it can propagate errors and fail under data- or capacity-mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable, and Context‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically supported family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models. KD routinely yields compact, deployable models that recover much of teacher performance when it is applied as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness. Real-world success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of known failure modes such as bias propagation and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Norman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Core but Not a Standalone Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical family of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across modalities, but its success depends on careful, task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression and data strategies. The recommended practice is to treat KD as a configurable, central component embedded in an integrated compression pipeline rather than as a turnkey cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods span soft-target/logit matching, representation- and attention-level objectives, relational and contrastive signals, and a variety of training protocols (offline, online/co-distillation, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware variants). Empirical evidence shows KD often enables substantial gains in latency, memory, and deployment cost while recovering much of teacher performance, but reliable application depends on task-aware choices about transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and combination with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Versatile, and Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques — spanning soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-representation matching, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and teacher-aware or multi-teacher strategies — repeatedly enable large reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on task and data properties, teacher–student alignment, optimization, and deployment constraints, and it works best when combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Context‑Dependent Path for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically powerful approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining most of the teacher performance. Its effectiveness stems from diverse ways of transferring information (logits, intermediate features, relational structure), flexible training protocols (offline, online, self-, multi-teacher), and the ability to combine with complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal remedy: success depends on signal choice, data availability and quality, teacher-student pairing, and careful integration with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task‑aware practices.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Empirical and methodological work shows KD enables practical deployment across modalities and constrained settings, but its success depends on careful design choices, complementary compression primitives, and explicit safeguards against transferred errors and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Vaughan
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive structure), how transfer is organized (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, or data‑free), and how they are integrated with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, neural architecture search, progressive module replacement). When carefully applied and combined with task‑aware choices about data, layer alignment, and auxiliary compression, KD frequently yields compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, KD is context dependent: success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and mitigation of failure modes such as propagation of teacher errors, degraded rare‑token behavior, distribution shift, and privacy concerns. The field emphasizes engineering pipelines that pair KD with complementary strategies and targeted remedies rather than a single universal recipe.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware, and Complementary Tool for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teachers into compact students. KD routinely enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, and supports a spectrum of signals and training protocols. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and distribution shift. I argue that KD should be treated as a central, configurable component of compression pipelines—powerful when combined with complementary methods and careful engineering, but requiring task‑aware safeguards to be reliable in production.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Dependent Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic pathway to compress large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations. Empirical work across vision, speech, language, multimodal and graph domains shows KD can retain much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory when combined with complementary compression tools. However, real-world success requires careful choice of teacher signals, data strategies, and optimization protocols to address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and modality or deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful, practical family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD uses diverse signals and training paradigms and is most effective when embedded in an integrated compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the available data regime (including synthesized or data‑free approaches), and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, capacity mismatch, and degraded handling of rare or out‑of‑distribution phenomena. Remaining challenges include principled signal selection for heterogeneous architectures, robust and private data‑free distillation, and automated, deployment‑aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Foley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, First‑Line Tool — Powerful but Not Sufficient for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible family of techniques that routinely enables compact, efficient models to inherit much of the behavior and performance of larger teacher models across vision, language, reinforcement learning, and healthcare applications. However, KD is context-sensitive: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and alignment, student capacity and architecture, the data or synthetic-data strategy used for transfer, and explicit defenses against propagated biases or rare-case failures. The best practical outcomes treat KD as a configurable, task-aware core within an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-level objectives, data strategies (including data-free or adversarial synthesis when needed), and complementary primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller, more deployable student models. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft-target (logit) supervision to intermediate-feature, attention, relational, and contrastive objectives—and is widely used across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal settings to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under memory or latency constraints, and support domain adaptation or privacy-aware releases. Practical success with KD depends on careful choice of what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, data availability (or synthesis), and combining distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware modifications. Remaining challenges include teacher imperfection and bias transfer, data scarcity and distribution shift, rare-token or rare-behavior degradation, and principled methods for heterogeneous architectures and automated objective selection.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Central, but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students. When combined with complementary compression primitives, careful choice of distillation targets and protocols, and task- or data-aware design, KD routinely produces compact models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability or synthesis strategy, and attention to robustness, low-frequency phenomena, and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a flexible toolkit that must be adapted to deployment constraints and complemented with privacy-, fairness-, and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, diverse family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or composite teacher models into smaller, faster, or more deployable student models. The field has evolved from matching soft output probabilities to include feature- and layer-level imitation, attention and relational transfer, contrastive and adversarial objectives, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols, and online or multi-teacher schemes. KD is effective across modalities and tasks (vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and multimodal systems) and often forms part of a broader compression pipeline together with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD success depends on task-aware choices—teacher quality, student capacity, the distillation signal, and the data available—and several practical challenges remain, including distribution shift, data heterogeneity (especially in federated settings), low-frequency/rare-token behavior, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Efficient and Robust Deep Models: Evidence, Techniques, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher→student transfer recipe into a broad set of methods that enable model compression, robustness, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving training, and architectural search. Across modalities and tasks—NLP, speech, vision, graphs, ranking and recommender systems—KD-based approaches consistently trade minimal performance loss for large gains in speed, memory, interpretability or deployability. The diversity of KD formulations (feature-based, layer-mapping, data-free, online/mutual, multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, and task-adaptive compression) provides practitioners with targeted tools to address constraints such as limited data, non-iid federated shards, low-frequency tokens in translation, and privacy requirements. Based on empirical results across the literature, KD should be considered a first-order technique in any pipeline that must deliver high-quality models under resource, privacy, or latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bailey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while often preserving much of the original performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) and across multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, and data‑free/synthetic data). Empirical work across vision, speech, and language shows KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs when combined with appropriate architecture alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical application treats KD as a configurable, context‑sensitive element of an integrated compression pipeline; its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and complexity, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Cervantes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Essential, Powerful, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models. Empirical evidence across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs. Successful distillation depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data availability and preparation, and integration with complementary compression methods. Treated as a toolbox—combining soft-targets with representation matching, progressive schedules, curriculum selection, and pruning/quantization—KD is a first‑order approach for real‑world compression when practitioners explicitly address its known limitations.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized models by transferring information from larger or alternative teacher models. KD variants include offline teacher-student distillation, online mutual distillation, ensemble-to-student distillation, cross-task distillation, and teacher-aware or student-aware training. Beyond the canonical logit-matching objective, modern work distills intermediate representations, relational and contrastive structures, and task-specific signals to improve accuracy, robustness, fairness, privacy, generation, and inference latency. Empirical results across computer vision, speech, machine translation, retrieval, graph learning, and routing problems show KD can both compress models without large accuracy loss and improve distilled students in multiple dimensions (robustness, fairness, generalization, and deployment cost). However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled knowledge (logits vs features vs relations), data complexity, and careful training strategies (sample selection, curriculum, annealing, or joint teacher-student learning). This synthesis summarizes methods, motivations, practical techniques, and empirical patterns observed across recent studies.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller students. Across modalities and training protocols, distillation operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware design. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability or synthesis, and careful objective and optimization design; important limitations include teacher error propagation, impaired modeling of low-frequency phenomena, and distribution-shift vulnerabilities.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural information. A broad toolkit of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals), protocols (offline, online/self-, multi-teacher, data‑free) and engineering practices (layer mapping, projectors, curriculum, data synthesis) has been developed and routinely combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirically, distillation frequently recovers most of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and augmentation strategies, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors or low-frequency phenomena. Effective deployment requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to integrate distillation within end-to-end compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, practical toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. A diverse set of distillation signals and training protocols—ranging from logits/soft labels to feature- and attention-level matching, contrastive and relational objectives, ensemble and online schemes, and data‑free or privacy-preserving techniques—are routinely combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search. Empirical evidence shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while producing substantial efficiency gains, but practical success is context dependent and requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability, and mitigation of transferred failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Jenkins
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and deployment constraints. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable element inside integrated compression pipelines and emphasize targeted evaluation of robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Research and practice have developed a diverse toolkit — matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features and attention, using contrastive/relational objectives, generating or selecting distillation data, multi-teacher and online schemes, and combining KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, speech, and multimodal tasks shows distilled students frequently recover much of teacher performance, though effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and alignment of objectives and representations. Key open problems include reliable transfer of rare or structured behaviors, robust distillation under data heterogeneity and privacy constraints, principled teacher selection and co-design, and automated, task-aware distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applied family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods (logits, features, attention, relational, contrastive, multi‑teacher, online/self and data‑free variants) are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation to meet deployment constraints, but their success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful protocol design.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and complementary model-compression techniques form a practical toolbox for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Methods vary by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel information, relational structures), whether real training data are available, and whether the goal is efficiency, robustness, privacy, or domain adaptation. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen distillation targets, layer-mapping strategies, teacher selection (including ensembles), and combinations with pruning or architecture-aware compression can recover much of teacher performance and enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include handling low-frequency phenomena, distributional mismatch in data-free or federated settings, and optimization or alignment difficulties between teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be adopted as the default first-line strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP, but only when deployed as a configurable, context-sensitive component inside an integrated compression pipeline. Remaining priorities include principled theory, robust distillation under scarce or private data, automation of teacher–student alignment, and preservation of long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Maynard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and deployment complexity. papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically validated framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data strategy (including synthetic or public data when originals are unavailable), and task-aware objective design. Treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline rather than a single recipe, KD is an essential practical tool for model deployment under resource, privacy, and latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ellis

papers_seen.author: Green

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Ubiquitous, but Demand-Aware
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for compressing high-capacity models into efficient students across modalities and tasks. Carefully chosen distillation algorithms and extensions (self-supervised distillation, meta-learned teachers, multi-teacher weighting, online and distributed schemes, and privacy-preserving perturbations) can mitigate common failure modes and broaden KD’s applicability in production and research settings.

papers_seen.author: Fields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Tool — Argument for Integrated, Context‑Aware Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, broadly applicable set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal tasks shows KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s effectiveness is conditional: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals, and the availability or synthesis of suitable training data. For robust, real‑world compression, KD should be treated as a configurable component within an integrated pipeline that combines representation-level transfer, data and curriculum strategies, and architecture‑aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search), together with explicit safeguards for bias, robustness, and low‑frequency behavior.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while often preserving much of task performance. KD is a flexible family of techniques that operate at output, representation, relational, or decision-boundary levels and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful design of objectives and training pipelines.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated paradigm for producing compact, deployable models by transferring behavior and internal representations from larger or composite teachers into smaller students. Across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and multimodal tasks, KD variants and protocols enable substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with task‑aware design, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression primitives. Practical deployment requires treating KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and addressing persistent limitations such as teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity, bias propagation, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practically oriented family of techniques for transferring information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or more deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, recommender systems, and other domains, KD has been adapted to operate at output, feature, and relational levels and combined with complementary compression primitives to meet resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of teacher performance, but success is conditional on choices about teacher signals, student capacity and architecture, the availability and match of distillation data, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as a central, configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a one-shot universal remedy.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely used family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft logits to intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive signals—and supports varied training protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, and data‑free variants). While KD routinely delivers meaningful efficiency gains with modest performance loss, reliable deployment requires integrating distillation with task‑aware design choices, complementary compression primitives, and explicit strategies to mitigate limitations such as data scarcity, teacher bias, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and broadly effective set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD reduces latency, memory, and communication costs while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance; its toolbox includes soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocols ranging from offline to online, multi-teacher, and data-free distillation. However, KD’s success is conditional on task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Responsible, robust deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline rather than as a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Power, Limits, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large models into lightweight students for deployment across vision, speech, graph, and NLP tasks. KD variants transfer information via logits, intermediate features, or data synthesized from teachers; they can also be combined with privacy or fairness measures. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, dataset mismatches, and design choices (what to mimic, which layers, how to align teacher and student) strongly affect outcomes. Careful method selection—feature vs. logit supervision, layer alignment, projector usage, sample selection, and teacher adaptation—enables consistent gains while meeting constraints like limited data, privacy, or fairness.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. The literature converges on a diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure, decision-boundary samples), training protocols (single/multi-teacher, teacher-annealing, self- or online-distillation, data-free or synthetic-data approaches), and architecture-aware adaptations (many-to-many layer mapping, projector adapters, and combinations with pruning/quantization). Empirical studies across vision, language, speech, multimodal, and generative tasks show distilled students can recover much teacher performance and sometimes yield superior efficiency–accuracy trade-offs; nonetheless, open problems remain around data scarcity and privacy, teacher–student mismatch, preserving low-frequency behaviors, and transferring robustness and fairness properties.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to satisfy deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD includes a wide set of objectives and training protocols (logits/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, online/multi-teacher schemes, and data‑free or synthesized-data approaches). Empirical work shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance when it is matched to student capacity and data regimes and when it is integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). At the same time, KD has clear limits—teacher–student mismatch, scarce or mismatched data, propagation of teacher errors and biases, and difficulty preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors—so best practice treats KD as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline with explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques reduce model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, cheaper models (students). Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed logit- and feature-level distillation, layer-wise and many-to-many layer matching, task-aware filtering, projector-based adapters, meta-learned teachers, multi-teacher weighting, and data- or privacy-constrained workflows. Empirical work demonstrates that carefully designed distillation protocols can retain much of teacher performance (and sometimes improve generalization) while enabling deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy; theoretical analyses offer insight into when soft labels help and when hard labels are necessary. Remaining challenges include bridging capacity gaps, dealing with mismatched architectures and modalities, operating without original data, and guaranteeing privacy under compression.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or more deployable student models. The literature converges on a rich taxonomy of distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, contrastive or relational objectives), training protocols (offline, online, self-distillation, data‑free or generator‑assisted), and architecture-aware adaptations (projectors, many‑to‑many layer mappings, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, retrieval, and multimodal settings shows distilled students can recover a large fraction of teacher performance and unlock deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s effectiveness is context dependent: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and match of distillation data, and explicit mitigations for bias, low‑frequency phenomena, and distribution shift. Key open directions include improved theory for diverse objectives, robust data‑free and privacy‑preserving distillation, principled automated teacher–student alignment for heterogeneous architectures, and joint optimization with complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful, practical family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD uses diverse signals and training paradigms and is most effective when embedded in an integrated compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the available data regime (including synthesized or data‑free approaches), and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, capacity mismatch, and degraded handling of rare or out‑of‑distribution phenomena. Remaining challenges include principled signal selection for heterogeneous architectures, robust and private data‑free distillation, and automated, deployment‑aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Hampton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and empirically supported set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. KD has been shown across modalities to produce compact models that recover much of teacher performance when properly configured. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (or synthesis), and integration with complementary compression methods. Because KD is not a universal cure, best practice treats it as a configurable component within an integrated compression pipeline that is adapted to task, data regime, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central and versatile toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. A broad family of distillation objectives and protocols has been developed—ranging from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature, attention, relational, contrastive, adversarial, and data‑free approaches—and KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and explicit handling of distribution shift, low-frequency behaviors, privacy, and architecture heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for transferring behavior and representations from large teacher models to smaller student models. When applied with appropriate objectives, layer mappings, data strategies, and safeguards, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and communication while preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: it interacts with teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, distribution shift, and fairness concerns. Treating KD as a configurable core of a compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, curriculum strategies, and privacy-aware protocols—yields the most reliable deployment outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Component of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirically validated and flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables deployment across modalities when integrated thoughtfully with complementary compression methods. Its success is context dependent — determined by teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and loss of rare behaviors — so practitioners should treat KD as a configurable element of a broader compression pipeline rather than a one-shot solution.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. The literature shows that appropriately chosen distillation signals, teacher–student design, and data strategies allow compact models to recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and adapt to constraints such as privacy, heterogeneous devices, and limited or unlabeled data. Despite widespread empirical success, important limitations persist—teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatch, degraded rare-output behavior, and theoretical gaps linking distillation signals to student generalization—motivating ongoing work in adaptive teacher selection, data-free distillation, and task-aware compression design.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in vision, language, multimodal, and other settings. KD encompasses a family of transfer signals and training protocols that, when chosen and tuned for task constraints and student capacity, frequently recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical deployments treat KD as a configurable component within integrated compression pipelines that also include pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies; success depends on teacher quality, the student’s capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as transferred bias, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques that are often the first and most effective instrument for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD methods now operate across multiple levels of supervision (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals) and protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, data‑free), and they are most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and tailored to task, data, and deployment constraints. However, the value of KD is conditional: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data regime, and mitigation of bias and distribution‑shift risks determine success. Consequently, best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey cure.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of the performance and functionality of larger teacher models. KD is highly versatile—operating at the level of logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational objectives—and is effective across modalities (vision, language, speech, recommender systems, and generative models). However, its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and distribution, and the design of distillation objectives; consequently KD should be treated as a configurable component that is combined with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical evidence across vision and language shows KD can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on careful choices about what information is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be treated as the central element of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a sole solution.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Context‑Sensitive, and Best Used in Hybrid Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven technique for converting large teacher models into smaller, efficient students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD reliably reduces latency, memory, and energy costs and can transfer robustness or domain knowledge, but it is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher and student design, data regime, and deployment constraints. For robust, deployable compression, KD is best treated as a configurable core component within integrated pipelines that combine representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their capabilities. KD enables deployment across modalities and constrained environments, and empirical work shows it can approach teacher performance when combined with complementary techniques. However, KD is not a universal solution: it can propagate teacher errors and biases, struggle under data scarcity or mismatch, and require careful choices of distilled targets, architectures, and training schedules. To realize KD's benefits in production and research settings, practitioners should pair distillation with targeted remedies—representation-aware objectives, data-and-curriculum strategies, ensemble or adversarial schemes, and fairness or privacy interventions—tailored to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Tool for Practical Deep Learning and NLP: Evidence, Methods, and Remaining Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for transferring capabilities from large teacher models into smaller student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving much of teacher performance. A large body of work develops variants that match logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, supports multi-teacher and teacher‑free regimes, and combines distillation with data augmentation, adversarial synthesis, or architectural adaptations. Despite robust practical gains, important open problems remain in data‑scarce or privacy‑constrained distillation, transferring fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors, principled layer mapping for heterogeneous architectures, and fairness- and robustness-aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, flexible family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure) and operate under varied protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free and privacy‑aware). Empirically, KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, latency, and memory, but its reliability is context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, choice or synthesis of distillation data, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness and privacy substantially affect outcomes. Practical use therefore treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline that combines appropriate distillation objectives with complementary compression techniques and targeted mitigations for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. Across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative modeling, researchers transfer information via softened output distributions, intermediate-feature matching, relational and attention maps, and many-to-many layer alignment. Variants address resource heterogeneity, data unavailability, privacy, robustness, and fairness. Empirical and analytic work shows that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, but its success depends on design choices (what to transfer, teacher quality, data or pseudo-data, and alignment losses). State-of-the-art practice mixes logits-based loss with feature- or representation-level objectives, task-aware augmentations, and architecture- or training-aware modifications to obtain favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective set of methods for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can operate under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD methods span soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher protocols, and data-free or few-shot schemes. Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks indicates KD routinely preserves a large fraction of teacher performance when applied with task-aware design, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability or synthesis of data, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as propagated bias, degraded low‑frequency behavior, and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable element within an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary primitives like pruning, quantization, and architecture search.
