papers_seen.author: Kline
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into compact student models. The literature provides a rich toolbox—output-level (soft targets), intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and variants such as multi-teacher, online/self-distillation, data‑free and meta‑learning approaches. Empirical and conceptual work agrees that KD is most effective when adapted to task constraints, student capacity, and data availability and when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design).

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language modalities, KD variants (logit matching, feature/attention matching, data-free/adversarial synthesis, multi-teacher and self-distillation) enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, avoidance of bias propagation, and principled design choices for heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression (but Not a Standalone Cure)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, and data-free variants), and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, retrieval, detection, and healthcare shows KD routinely enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and careful objective and architecture design. Best practice treats KD as the central, configurable element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that explicitly addresses data scarcity, distribution shift, privacy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression and Transfer: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile set of techniques that enable model compression, domain- and task-level transfer, privacy-preserving distillation, and improvements in interpretability and fairness. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can compress large models into efficient students, transfer inductive biases, support multi-task and lifelong learning, and enable data-free or zero-shot distillation when training data are unavailable. At the same time, KD faces concrete limitations due to data heterogeneity, teacher-student capacity mismatch, and the need to select or synthesize appropriate supervision; hybrid solutions that combine feature-level matching, adversarial sample synthesis, curriculum strategies, and architectural compression achieve the best practical results. Based on evidence across domains (vision, language, graphs, retrieval, reinforcement learning), we argue that KD should be used as part of an integrated compression pipeline that is task-aware, data-aware, and often combined with pruning, layer skipping, or module replacement to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Meza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of KD objectives and workflows—ranging from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature alignment, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation, data‑free and adversarial approaches, and projector or curriculum-based engineering—has been developed and applied across vision and language tasks. Distillation enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints but is not universally guaranteed: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of transfer signals and training procedures. The practical consensus is to treat KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated paradigm for producing compact, deployable models by transferring behavior and internal representations from larger or composite teachers into smaller students. Across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and multimodal tasks, KD variants and protocols enable substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with task‑aware design, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression primitives. Practical deployment requires treating KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and addressing persistent limitations such as teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity, bias propagation, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and practical family of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while often preserving much of a teacher’s performance, but it is not a standalone cure: success depends on careful choices of transfer targets, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. For reliable deployment, KD should be treated as a configurable, task‑aware core of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-aware objectives, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design).

papers_seen.author: Griffin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of techniques for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD reliably reduces latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance in many settings, but its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy. For production-grade compression, KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated pipeline rather than a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques for transferring information from larger or richer models (teachers) into smaller, more efficient models (students). KD methods range from matching teacher output distributions to aligning internal representations and using synthesized or privatized data; they are effective across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks and are commonly integrated with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while improving inference cost, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and safeguards against propagating undesirable teacher properties. Current practice treats KD as a configurable component of wider compression pipelines rather than a single algorithm, and several methodological extensions and safeguards have been proposed to address its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Core, Conditional, and Configurable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable, task‑aware component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, or multi-teacher ensembles), KD routinely delivers large reductions in latency and memory while preserving most teacher performance. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy; KD is therefore best used as a first-line, integrated tool rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a logits-matching trick into a broad, practical framework for shrinking and adapting large models while retaining much of their performance. Modern KD techniques include soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and ensemble-teacher schemes, online and distributed formulations, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Across vision, language, recommendation, and domain-adaptation settings, KD is most effective when combined with complementary strategies (pretraining, pruning, quantization, curriculum or online training, and task-aware losses). Despite strong empirical successes, practitioners must attend to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and domain mismatch; many current research directions focus on robust, privacy-preserving, and data-limited distillation for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Shah
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. KD supports multiple transfer targets and training protocols, is routinely combined with other compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and has been applied across modalities (language, vision, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks). Its empirical success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and careful design of what and how to transfer; persistent challenges include robustness, privacy, and reliable transfer of rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, empirically supported family of techniques that should be treated as the central, configurable component of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP. When designed with task- and deployment-awareness and combined with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data strategies), KD routinely produces compact students that recover most teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not sufficient on its own: achieving reliable, deployment-grade compression requires deliberate teacher–student alignment, data-aware protocols, and explicit mitigations for transferred errors, fairness, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Burgess
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD methods include output-level supervision, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, online and multi-teacher protocols, and progressive or task-aware procedures. Empirical work across vision, language, retrieval, generative and multimodal tasks shows that when KD is integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with task- and data-aware engineering, it often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing resource cost. Practical success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Important open challenges remain in principled selection of distillation targets, reliable transfer under data scarcity and distribution shift, avoiding propagation of teacher biases and rare-token degradation, and automated, hardware-aware co-design.

papers_seen.author: Summers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models or ensembles into smaller, deployable student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while retaining much of task performance. Modern KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis. KD is commonly combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence indicates KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and suitable data strategies are aligned, but its success is context-dependent and requires task-aware design to mitigate limits related to teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger or multi-modal models to smaller or specialized models to reduce inference cost, enable deployment in constrained environments, and improve robustness or fairness. Across computer vision, natural language processing, speech, recommender systems, graph learning, generative modelling, and multimodal tasks, a broad set of mechanisms—soft-label supervision, feature- and attention-level matching, multi-teacher and ensemble methods, online/peer-distillation, and task- or domain-specific adaptations—have been developed. Empirical results demonstrate that distillation can yield compact models that approach teacher performance, accelerate training or inference, improve small-model self-supervised learning, and enable modality transfer, while theoretical and empirical analyses highlight factors that govern success: student capacity, teacher imperfection, data complexity, data augmentation, and bias-variance tradeoffs. Open challenges remain in principled theory, privacy-preserving and fairness-aware distillation, and extending distillation reliably to generative and highly structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Rowe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, compute, and occasionally privacy constraints by matching teacher outputs, representations, or relational structure; it is routinely combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies (augmentation, synthetic data) to meet task- and deployment-specific requirements. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance, its success is context dependent and requires careful choices about distillation targets, teacher–student alignment, and data handling; open problems remain in principled target selection, robustness to distribution shift and rare outputs, and automated teacher–student matching.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Across modalities and tasks, a diverse toolkit — including logits/soft-target matching, feature- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, online and data-free protocols, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design — has been shown to deliver large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when applied with task-aware engineering. Important remaining challenges include theoretical understanding of what is transferred, robust and private distillation under data scarcity or distribution shift, and reliably preserving fine-grained or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be adopted as the default first-line strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP, but only when deployed as a configurable, context-sensitive component inside an integrated compression pipeline. KD routinely yields compact students that recover much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks; however, reliable, deployment-grade outcomes require explicit attention to what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) plus safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining priorities include principled theory, robust distillation under scarce or private data, automation of teacher–student alignment, and preservation of long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hester
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically proven family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely improves efficiency (latency, memory, compute) while often recovering a large fraction of teacher performance, but its success is conditional: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, distilled signals, data regime, and explicit mitigation of failure modes determine outcomes. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies, and robustness/privacy safeguards) rather than a turn‑key cure.

papers_seen.author: Erickson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Findings, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied and empirically supported family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models. KD methods include soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and variants for online, multi-teacher, data-free, and privacy-aware regimes. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation/search) and task-aware choices about what to transfer and how to map layers, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving a large fraction of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architectural alignment, available data (or synthesis strategies), and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, degraded low-frequency or out-of-distribution behavior, and privacy concerns. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable core of integrated compression pipelines and motivates several active research directions including principled teacher–student co-design, robust and private distillation under limited data, and theory linking distilled signals to student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression (but Not a Standalone Solution)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, flexible technique for producing compact, deployable models in deep learning and NLP by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teachers to smaller students. KD routinely delivers strong reductions in latency, memory, and parameter footprint while preserving a large portion of teacher performance when configured to task and deployment constraints. However, KD has concrete failure modes—capacity mismatch, teacher artifact transfer, degraded low-frequency performance, and sensitivity to data availability and distribution shift—and therefore is best applied as a configurable core within an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline that includes complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), data and curriculum strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Li
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Configurable, but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically proven family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students to meet deployment constraints in deep learning and NLP. KD improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs by transferring soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure, and can operate in offline, online, multi‑teacher, data‑free, and privacy‑sensitive regimes. However, its effectiveness depends on deliberate choices about transfer targets, teacher–student co‑design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives; without such integration KD risks failing under teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or distribution shift, optimization challenges, and the propagation of undesirable behaviors. This position argues that KD should be treated as the core, configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline: necessary for most modern deployments but insufficient on its own, and requiring targeted practices and continued research to address open challenges.

papers_seen.author: Shepherd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically supported toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants (logit/soft-target matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-aware workflows) consistently enable favorable trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and model size. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, availability and match of data, and distribution shift shape outcomes. For robust, production-ready compression, KD should be configured and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design), data strategies, and task-aware safeguards against bias and low-frequency failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, widely adopted family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Across modalities and tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature-, attention-, relational- and adversarial-level objectives, as well as online, multi-teacher, and data-free variants—routinely reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Documented success is context-sensitive: effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and distribution, and careful selection of distillation targets and complementary compression methods; ongoing challenges include principled objective selection, reliable distillation under limited or mismatched data, and mitigation of transferred biases and robustness/fairness issues.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: The Promise and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central method for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, KD variants enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, promote interpretable surrogates, and support ensemble compression. However, KD also transfers teacher biases, faces optimization and data-distribution challenges, and requires careful choices of objectives, data augmentation, and teacher-student protocols to be effective in practice.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and versatile family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers, but it is not a standalone cure-all. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and representations across modalities when chosen and tuned with regard to teacher quality, student capacity, data regimes, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies—while adopting safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, researchers have extended KD beyond soft-label matching to include feature- and attention-level alignment, contrastive and relational objectives, online and self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Practical success depends on teacher quality and student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthetic-data strategies, and combinations with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of when particular signals help, handling heterogeneous or non-iid data in federated settings, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and reliably scaling distillation in large distributed systems.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes empirical findings, methodological variants, use-cases, limitations, and practical recommendations for knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques in deep learning and NLP. Drawing solely on the provided studies, it highlights common transfer targets and training regimes, domain- and task-specific adaptations, and recurring failure modes, and offers guidance on when and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or specialized student models. KD methods—ranging from soft-target (logit) transfer to intermediate feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer mappings, adversarial ensemble compression, and privacy-aware protocols—enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints while often improving student generalization. Practical success depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity and task needs, choosing or synthesizing suitable data, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Key challenges remain in handling teacher imperfection and bias, data- and domain-shift, low-frequency/structured outputs, and providing principled guarantees for fairness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Browning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Aware Component of Practical Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated technique for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers across vision, language, recommender, and multimodal tasks. KD routinely delivers substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss when applied with task- and capacity-aware design, but it is not a universal remedy: its success depends on choices of transfer signal, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and loss of rare behaviors. For reliable production use, KD should be treated as a configurable core element within hybrid compression pipelines that include pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data-aware safeguards.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency across vision and NLP. However, KD alone rarely solves all deployment challenges: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and objective design. The most reliable practice treats KD as a configurable core component embedded within integrated compression pipelines that combine representation alignment, data or data‑free strategies, and architecture- and hardware-aware methods.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central Utility, Practical Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable technique for transferring capabilities from large teacher models into compact student models so that high-performing systems can run under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, features, attention, relations) and training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free) and is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to produce deployable models. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on task-aware choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and explicit handling of bias, low-frequency behavior, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD reliably reduces latency and parameter counts while preserving much of teacher performance when its objectives, data strategy, and teacher–student alignment are chosen with task and deployment constraints in mind. However, KD is not a universal solution: capacity mismatch, teacher errors and biases, limited or private data, and optimization instability limit off‑the‑shelf success. The strongest practical outcomes arise when KD is treated as a configurable core within hybrid compression pipelines that also employ pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task‑aware data procedures.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behaviors and internal representations. A wide palette of distillation targets and protocols — from soft logits to intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive structures, adversarial or data-free schemes, and multi‑teacher or self‑distillation — has been developed and applied across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. Empirical findings show KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can enable favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when integrated with complementary compression techniques and appropriate data strategies. Nonetheless, KD’s effectiveness is context dependent, shaped by teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and composition, and persistent issues such as distribution shift, low‑frequency/long‑tail behaviors, privacy leakage, and bias propagation.

papers_seen.author: Mendoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Effects, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, flexible framework for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals) and protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free, and curriculum-driven). Empirical work demonstrates KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthesis, and integration with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all. Key open directions include principled selection of signals to transfer, robust privacy-preserving distillation, automation of deployment-aware pipelines, and reliable compression of large transformer and generative models.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or hardware‑optimal compression; its effectiveness depends on careful, task‑aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to integrate complementary compression methods. Treating KD as the central element within an engineered pipeline — augmented by teacher selection, data strategies, and pruning/quantization or architecture adaptations — delivers the most reliable outcomes for real deployments.

A broad set of methods—logit-level transfer, feature- and relation-level matching, adversarial and data-free protocols, and task-aware adaptations—enables KD to serve as a first-order component of practical compression pipelines. papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners transfer logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or decision-boundary information and combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation) to meet latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often recover most teacher performance and, in some cases, match or exceed teachers when distillation is paired with careful teacher design, layer mapping, and data or training schedules. Major limitations remain in imperfect belief matching, distribution shift, handling low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous or privacy-constrained data, and principled teacher selection—areas where methodological and theoretical progress continues to be needed.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, broadly applicable framework for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' utility. KD methods span output matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, self- and ensemble-distillation, meta-learned and student-friendly teacher designs, and data- or task-aware adaptations. Empirical work across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks demonstrates KD’s ability to deliver large reductions in model size and compute with modest performance loss, and in many cases to improve robustness or generalization when combined with appropriate procedures. At the same time, KD’s reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; addressing these constraints through architectural design, curriculum and meta-learning, augmentation and synthetic-data strategies, and multi-teacher or online schemes is central to practical deployment.

Across vision, language, recommendation, speech, graph, and generative tasks, KD variants enable substantial reductions in parameter count, latency, and memory while often retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. Practical success is context dependent: it requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, which data or synthetic samples to use, and how to pair KD with complementary compression methods and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining challenges include distilling in data-scarce or privacy-sensitive regimes, handling teacher–student architecture mismatch, and preserving long-tail or rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational, Task‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods span output-level supervision, intermediate-representation matching, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and many-to-many layer mappings, and are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. When applied with task-awareness — i.e., selecting appropriate distilled signals, matching teacher and student capacity, and adapting data and optimization — KD reliably delivers favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision, language, speech, detection, and federated settings. Nevertheless, KD has well-documented failure modes (capacity and optimization gaps, bias transfer, degradation on rare phenomena, and privacy concerns), and future progress depends on principled theory, automation of teacher–student matching, and responsible, privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Configurable Core of Integrated Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically supported family of techniques that enables deployment of compact models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teachers. I argue that KD should be treated as a central, configurable component of integrated compression pipelines rather than a standalone cure: when combined with task‑aware choices about transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD reliably improves accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, its success is conditional on addressing persistent limitations — teacher quality and capacity mismatch, data scarcity and privacy constraints, propagation of biases and degraded rare‑token behaviors — which necessitate explicit mitigation, careful evaluation, and targeted future research.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Findings and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques provide a practical path to deploy high-performing deep models under resource, latency, privacy, and domain constraints. Across modalities, KD variants—soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate representation and attention alignment, adversarial or data-free schemes, and online/self-distillation—routinely yield compact students that recover much of a teacher's performance when combined with careful data, optimization, and architecture choices. Practical success requires embedding KD in an integrated compression pipeline and attending to teacher/student design, data regimes, and known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, recommendation, retrieval, multimodal, and federated settings, KD variants — from soft‑target (logit) matching to intermediate‑feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data‑synthesis or privacy‑aware protocols — routinely improve efficiency while retaining much of teacher performance when integrated into broader compression pipelines. Practical success is context dependent and hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability (or synthesis), objective design, and explicit handling of risks such as bias propagation, degraded low‑frequency behavior, and distributional shift. Remaining gaps include principled theory linking distillation choices to student generalization, robust and private data‑free distillation, and automated co‑design of students and distillation targets for heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Tool: Integrating Distillation with Representation, Data, and Architecture Strategies for Robust Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, more deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. However, KD alone is rarely sufficient to meet real-world deployment constraints: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled signals (logits, features, attention), and access to or synthesis of suitable training data. Best results arise when KD is embedded in an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-level matching, projector or layer-mapping modules, data and curriculum strategies, and architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or layer skipping). Careful attention to optimization, robustness, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors is required to avoid propagating teacher errors and to produce reliable compact models for downstream applications.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Treated as a configurable, task-aware core within an integrated compression pipeline and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies), KD routinely produces favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. Its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, degraded low-frequency behavior, and distribution shift. Effective, production‑ready compression therefore treats KD as essential but not sufficient: apply it thoughtfully, evaluate its downstream impacts, and combine it with targeted safeguards and complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Contextual Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, broadly applicable set of methods for producing smaller, faster, and deployment-ready models by transferring information from large teacher models into compact students. KD techniques range from soft-label (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and relational objectives, and they have been adapted to settings with limited or no original training data, to multi-teacher or online schemes, and to combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve interpretability or privacy-aware deployment, its success depends on task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and distributional constraints. Consequently, KD is best treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline rather than as a plug-and-play cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Versatile, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core technique for compressing large models and transferring their knowledge into smaller, faster models for deployment in resource-constrained settings and domain-specific applications. Advances in layer- and feature-level transfer, many-to-many layer mapping, data- and augmentation-aware practices, and federated or privacy-sensitive adaptations have expanded KD's applicability across vision, NLP, and graph domains. However, KD is not a universal remedy: it can propagate teacher errors, struggle under data heterogeneity, and depend critically on teacher quality, data choices, and optimization design. Best outcomes follow when practitioners combine KD with complementary techniques (careful layer matching, feature mimicking, data selection/augmentation, and pruning or quantization) and explicitly address heterogeneity and teacher reliability.

papers_seen.author: Gordon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of methods for producing compact models from larger teachers. Empirical work across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows KD can deliver large efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data and objective design, and complementary compression choices.

papers_seen.author: May

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations across modalities and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and careful choice of transfer signals; for robust, real-world compression KD should be treated as a configurable component of integrated pipelines that include complementary compression primitives and explicit safeguards for bias, robustness, and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations so that compact models meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A diverse toolkit has emerged — soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data strategies including data-free synthesis and targeted augmentation — which is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical work shows distilled students frequently recover a large fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and distillation data are aligned, but KD has documented limitations (teacher–student mismatch, degradation on low-frequency behaviors, bias and privacy transfer, and sensitivity under data scarcity or distribution shift). Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline, selecting distilled signals, data protocols, and complementary compression techniques according to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Stephenson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesized Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically validated family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD methods span soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-side strategies (including data-free and synthesized data). Reliable compression uses KD as a configurable core within hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and task-aware data and evaluation practices.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or more deployable student models. The literature converges on a rich taxonomy of distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, contrastive or relational objectives), training protocols (offline, online, self-distillation, data‑free or generator‑assisted), and architecture-aware adaptations (projectors, many‑to‑many layer mappings, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, retrieval, and multimodal settings shows distilled students can recover a large fraction of teacher performance and unlock deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s effectiveness is context dependent: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and match of distillation data, and explicit mitigations for bias, low‑frequency phenomena, and distribution shift. Key open directions include improved theory for diverse objectives, robust data‑free and privacy‑preserving distillation, principled automated teacher–student alignment for heterogeneous architectures, and joint optimization with complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision, language, multimodal and reinforcement settings, KD variants (soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives) and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, neural architecture search, data synthesis) enable practical deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover most teacher performance and, in some settings, exceed it, but success depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, choice of distillation targets, and targeted engineering such as projectors, pre-training for compact architectures, and curriculum or multi-teacher schemes.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely used family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft logits to intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive signals—and supports varied training protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, and data‑free variants). While KD routinely delivers meaningful efficiency gains with modest performance loss, reliable deployment requires integrating distillation with task‑aware design choices, complementary compression primitives, and explicit strategies to mitigate limitations such as data scarcity, teacher bias, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across modalities and tasks, distillation is used to transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from larger, more accurate teachers to smaller, faster students; it also appears within automated model search, pruning and distributed training workflows. Work in this area spans logit matching, representation-level objectives, data-free and few-shot regimes, multi-/online-teacher schemes, and task- or architecture-aware compression. Empirical results demonstrate that carefully designed distillation strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher accuracy while enabling large reductions in memory and compute, but limitations remain around optimization, data availability, and the preservation or mitigation of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Tool for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for transferring behavior from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses many targets and protocols and—when designed with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data, and complementary compression methods—regularly yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is not a universal remedy: careful protocol design, combination with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behaviors are required for dependable real‑world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Griffin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of techniques for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD reliably reduces latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance in many settings, but its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy. For production-grade compression, KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated pipeline rather than a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods provide practical routes to deploy high-performing deep models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints. The literature has developed diverse approaches that transfer information via soft logits, intermediate features, attentional maps, channel-wise statistics, and online mutual learning; adaptations address task-specific compression, data-free or few-shot regimes, large-scale distributed training, and teacher-student co-optimization. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, and that selecting what, when, and how to transfer knowledge (e.g., logits vs. features, offline vs. online, task-aware filtering) is crucial to achieve favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Aware Core of Integrated Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically grounded set of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal signals from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency. KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains across vision, language, and multimodal tasks when its objectives, teacher–student alignment, and data strategies are chosen with deployment constraints in mind. However, KD is context dependent and not a standalone panacea: reliable production use combines KD with complementary compression methods, careful data and objective design, and explicit mitigations for known failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagated biases, and degraded long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool that Requires Task-Aware, Complementary Engineering
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for producing compact models from large teachers that supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD reliably reduces inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher's performance, but its success depends on matching distillation objectives and procedures to task constraints and student capacity. Best outcomes arise when KD is treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes representation alignment, data- and task-aware strategies, and complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Gregory
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Considerations, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically validated family of techniques that transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of task performance. KD methods include soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, many-to-many layer mappings, and data- or privacy-aware variants. KD is most effective when designed as a task- and deployment-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline together with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; its empirical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and careful alignment between teacher and student. Remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, transfer of teacher biases, low-data or data-free regimes, principled layer mapping, and theoretical understanding of when and which distilled signals are most effective.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient — An Argument for Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely adopted approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. Empirical evidence across modalities shows KD routinely recovers much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of transferred signals, and availability or synthesis of appropriate data. For robust, fair, and production-ready compression, KD should operate as a configurable core within integrated pipelines that combine representation matching, data strategies, and architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or layer adaptation).

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. Across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative modeling, researchers transfer information via softened output distributions, intermediate-feature matching, relational and attention maps, and many-to-many layer alignment. Variants address resource heterogeneity, data unavailability, privacy, robustness, and fairness. Empirical and analytic work shows that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, but its success depends on design choices (what to transfer, teacher quality, data or pseudo-data, and alignment losses). State-of-the-art practice mixes logits-based loss with feature- or representation-level objectives, task-aware augmentations, and architecture- or training-aware modifications to obtain favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. Across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains, KD spans soft‑target/logit matching, intermediate‑feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocols including offline, online/self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free distillation. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs and can recover a large fraction of teacher performance when applied with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data regimes, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). However, KD’s effectiveness is context‑dependent: reliable deployment requires teacher–student co‑design, careful choice of distilled signals, appropriate data strategies, and mitigations for failure modes such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, distribution shift, and degradation on rare/low‑frequency phenomena. papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods operate at multiple levels — soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives — and in many training protocols (offline/online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data-free/zero‑shot schemes). Empirical results across vision and language show that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and appropriate data or synthesis strategies are addressed. Practical application treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of integrated compression pipelines (often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search), while explicit attention is required for limits such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, bias transfer, and degraded modeling of rare outputs.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. papers_seen.author: Williams

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers capabilities of large models into smaller ones via indirect supervision. papers_seen.author: Rodriguez

papers_seen.author: Daniel

However, the value of KD is conditional: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data regime, and mitigation of bias and distribution‑shift risks determine success. papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.
