papers_seen.author: Park
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target supervision to a configurable toolkit including intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher protocols, data‑free synthesis, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success is context-dependent and requires careful choices about teacher design, student capacity, data strategies, and mitigation of bias or distributional issues.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used framework for transferring predictive behavior from large, expensive teachers to smaller, efficient students. Across vision, language, recommendation, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD has been extended beyond logits-matching into feature and layer-level mimicry, online and self-distillation, adversarial and contrastive objectives, task-adaptive architecture search, and combinations with pruning and quantization. Empirical results show KD enables substantial latency and memory reductions while often preserving accuracy, improving calibration, and helping robustness; success depends strongly on choices about what to transfer, teacher quality, data and augmentation, and alignment strategies between heterogeneous models.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective family of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers. Its methods and protocols span soft-logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, ensemble and multi-teacher schemes, online and data-free variants, and task-specific adaptations. I argue KD should be treated as the central, configurable element of integrated compression pipelines whose design is driven by task constraints, data regimes, and deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for shrinking large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD routinely reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data availability. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core element within an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and task-aware data strategies—and couples it with explicit measures to mitigate bias, robustness failures, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Cooper
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Trade-offs, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models. KD methods span output-level supervision, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and multiple training protocols (offline, online/self, multi‑teacher, and data‑free). When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design/search) and task‑aware data strategies, KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks. However, success is context dependent: reliable distillation requires careful teacher–student design, appropriate data or synthesis strategies, and safeguards against propagated teacher errors, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, distribution shift, and privacy or fairness risks. Important open directions include principled theory of what transfers, robust/private distillation under limited or heterogeneous data, and methods for preserving structured or generative behaviors in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for producing compact models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD variants and complementary compression methods enable substantial reductions in computation, memory, and latency while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and integration with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. KD methods encompass soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and data‑free protocols, and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD frequently recovers a large portion of teacher performance and enables deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints, its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity, choice of distilled signals, and data regime. For robust, high-fidelity compression, KD is best treated as a configurable component of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline that includes safeguards and complementary techniques to address known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while preserving task performance. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and in multiple training regimes (offline teacher→student, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, recommender, and generative settings shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains when combined with task-aware choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning and quantization. However, KD is context dependent: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and mitigation of failure modes including propagation of teacher errors, degraded long‑tail behavior, and privacy risks. Treating KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline, and combining it with tailored safeguards and auxiliary methods, is the prevailing practical recommendation.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking model size and latency while preserving performance across computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation, and federated settings. Research has expanded beyond the original logits-matching paradigm into feature mimicking, many-to-many layer mapping, teacher engineering, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and task-adaptive compression. Empirical and theoretical work highlights important interactions between data complexity, teacher strength, inductive bias, and augmentation strategies, and identifies practical challenges including model-heterogeneity, data heterogeneity, and the need for robust data-free methods. The field increasingly emphasizes not only how to distill but also what to distill (logits, features, inter-class relations, view- or task-specific knowledge) and how to adapt distillation to application constraints (privacy, federated settings, domain shifts, resource budgets).

papers_seen.author: Olson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated family of techniques for transferring information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD supports a wide set of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals), training protocols (offline, online/self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free and few‑shot), and complementary compression mechanisms (pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD routinely produces strong efficiency–accuracy trade‑offs across modalities, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and careful selection of what and how to transfer; practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component within larger compression pipelines and pair it with task‑aware safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, graph, multimodal, and federated settings, a diverse set of distillation targets and training protocols have been developed to meet compute, memory, latency, privacy, and domain constraints. When designed in a task- and capacity-aware manner and combined with complementary compression methods, distillation often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance; however, important limitations remain, including teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, distribution shift, and trade-offs involving robustness and fairness. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, practical prescriptions, and the main open problems identified in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic for compressing neural networks into a broad, practically validated family of techniques for producing compact models that retain much of the functionality of larger teachers. KD methods transfer information via outputs, intermediate features, relational signals, or synthesized data, and they are applied across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, multimodal) and problem classes (classification, detection, generation, reinforcement learning, segmentation, view synthesis). Practical success depends on matching the distillation strategy to the task and deployment constraints (data availability, privacy, capacity, latency, hardware), and on integrating KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware adaptations. Remaining challenges include teacher imperfections, capacity mismatch, limited or private data, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviour in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible, but Not Panacea Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students and for transferring task- or modality-specific capabilities. KD supports many transfer targets and training protocols and can be combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and data synthesis to meet deployment constraints. However, reliable outcomes require careful teacher–student design, attention to data and privacy constraints, and targeted solutions for failure modes such as distribution shift, optimization mismatch, and preserved low-frequency behavior.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes the state of knowledge distillation (KD) as a core set of techniques for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. It surveys common distillation targets and protocols, empirical patterns of when KD succeeds or fails, practical integrations with other compression primitives, and recurring open challenges. The goal is to provide practitioners and researchers with a concise, evidence-based view of what KD reliably achieves and which design choices matter most for deployable model compression.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression (but Not a Standalone Cure)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, and data-free variants), and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, retrieval, detection, and healthcare shows KD routinely enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and careful objective and architecture design. Best practice treats KD as the central, configurable element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that explicitly addresses data scarcity, distribution shift, privacy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely successful family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost, but its reliability depends on task- and data-aware design choices, teacher–student alignment, and integration with complementary compression primitives. Responsible deployment requires explicit attention to data availability, distributional shift, rare-case behaviors, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations through multiple signals and training protocols, and they are most effective when integrated with task‑aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives. KD routinely enables large efficiency gains but requires careful handling of teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and known failure modes for robust, deployable compression.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a versatile family of techniques for transferring behavior, representations, or relational structure from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and online/self- or multi-teacher protocols—are widely used across vision, language, speech, multimodal and federated settings. When combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, effectiveness is context-dependent: KD success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and explicit mitigation of propagated biases, low-frequency failures, and distribution shift. Continued progress requires principled theory, robust data- and privacy-aware distillation, automated teacher–student co-design, and practical safeguards for fairness and rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Rush
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable, and Conditional Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques that enables production of compact, deployable models by transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities when its signals, data, and training protocols are chosen to match task and deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey cure: its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and alignment, and integration with complementary compression primitives and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. I argue KD should be treated as a core, configurable element of compression pipelines and applied with targeted mitigations for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods provide practical routes to deploy high-performing deep models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints. The literature has developed diverse approaches that transfer information via soft logits, intermediate features, attentional maps, channel-wise statistics, and online mutual learning; adaptations address task-specific compression, data-free or few-shot regimes, large-scale distributed training, and teacher-student co-optimization. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, and that selecting what, when, and how to transfer knowledge (e.g., logits vs. features, offline vs. online, task-aware filtering) is crucial to achieve favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ruiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring behavior from large or ensemble teacher models to smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants — including soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free synthesis — are used alone or with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to reduce parameters, latency, and memory while attempting to retain teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to task and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and mitigating transferred biases or rare-case failures. Important open problems include teacher–student capacity gaps, domain shift and data scarcity, privacy guarantees for data-free and federated settings, and automated teacher–student co-design for hardware-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Versatile, but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports diverse transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), adapts to data-limited and privacy‑sensitive settings, and interoperates with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its empirical strengths make KD a first‑line approach for many deployment problems, but reliable, production‑grade compression requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data selection or synthesis, capacity matching, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD spans simple soft-target (logit) matching to richer objectives that align intermediate representations, attention maps, relational or contrastive structures, and decision boundaries; it also includes online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data‑free variants. Across vision, language, graphs, speech, detection, and generative modeling, KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and performance when it is matched to student capacity, teacher quality, and the available data. Practical success typically requires integrating KD into a broader compression pipeline (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis/augmentation) and explicitly addressing teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, distribution shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable behaviors. Key open directions include principled signal selection for heterogeneous architectures, robust data‑free and privacy‑preserving distillation, and automated, deployment‑aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Parrish
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated set of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble ‘‘teacher’’ models into smaller, deployable ‘‘student’’ models. The technique operates at multiple levels (output distributions, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, or via synthesized data) and is commonly combined with complementary compression mechanisms (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). KD routinely yields large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance when its signals, protocols, and data are chosen to match student capacity and task constraints. However, success is context dependent: teacher quality, student architecture and capacity, availability and selection of data (including data-free regimes), and explicit handling of fairness, privacy, and rare/low-frequency phenomena all shape outcomes. As a result, best practice treats KD as a configurable core of integrated compression pipelines rather than a single turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from softened-logit supervision to intermediate-feature matching, relational/contrastive objectives, and data-free or generator-driven protocols—routinely recover a large fraction of teacher performance when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression primitives. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies; consequently KD is most reliable when used as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, pretraining, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: The Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable students across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains. KD can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and progressive replacement to yield compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, teacher quality, and the choice of what and how to transfer. Addressing pitfalls such as harmful teacher supervision on particular samples, degraded signals for low-frequency outputs, data unavailability, privacy concerns, and fairness requires targeted strategies (selective distillation, adapted teachers, self-distillation, generative replay, or tailored objectives).

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applied family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods (logits, features, attention, relational, contrastive, multi‑teacher, online/self and data‑free variants) are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation to meet deployment constraints, but their success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful protocol design.

papers_seen.author: Ponce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models across vision, language, speech, and other modalities. KD methods operate over multiple signals and protocols and are most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that also addresses data, architecture, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Patton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a diverse, practically oriented toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller, more deployable student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—including soft-label (logit) transfer, intermediate feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and self-distillation, online and offline protocols, and data-free or privacy-aware techniques—have enabled substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. Effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data availability and domain match, and integration with complementary compression methods; open challenges remain around theory, robust data-free distillation, heterogeneous architectures, and mitigating transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Oneill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, objective design, and integration with complementary compression methods. Treating KD as a configurable component of a task-aware compression pipeline—with explicit attention to data, robustness, and fairness—yields the most reliable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Insufficient Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD enables deployment on resource-constrained devices, supports privacy-aware and data-limited settings, and generalizes across modalities (vision, language, graphs, and generative models). However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on the choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and complementary engineering (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and training pipelines). Reliable, high-quality compression therefore treats distillation as a core technique within a broader, task-aware compression strategy rather than as a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically essential family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, graph, generative, and multimodal tasks shows that KD can recover much of a teacher's performance while reducing parameters, latency, and memory. Successful use of KD is conditional: it requires task-aware selection of transfer targets and protocols, attention to teacher–student capacity and architectural alignment, appropriate data or synthesized examples, and combination with complementary compression methods and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, and multimodal settings. It can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, and it interacts naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, distillation's success depends on the distillation objective, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and task-specific considerations; when these are not addressed it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with rare outputs, or fail due to optimization issues. Best practice is to treat KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines—combining logits, intermediate feature matching, projector modules, multi-teacher or teacher-adaptive designs, and data-aware schedules—to maximize student utility in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Garrett
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically oriented family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Modern KD extends well beyond soft-target/logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, data-free or adversarial synthesis, and multi-teacher or online training regimes. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline — aligned to teacher and student architectures, data availability, and deployment constraints — and combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Important practical limits remain (teacher–student capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or bias, domain shift, and scarce or private data), motivating task-aware design choices, layer-mapping strategies, and privacy-preserving or data-synthesis approaches.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. The literature shows that appropriately chosen distillation signals, teacher–student design, and data strategies allow compact models to recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and adapt to constraints such as privacy, heterogeneous devices, and limited or unlabeled data. Despite widespread empirical success, important limitations persist—teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatch, degraded rare-output behavior, and theoretical gaps linking distillation signals to student generalization—motivating ongoing work in adaptive teacher selection, data-free distillation, and task-aware compression design.

papers_seen.author: Camacho
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When applied as a task-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline—alongside pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies—KD frequently yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, and the data regime.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Findings from the Provided Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under constraints of latency, memory, compute, and privacy. The literature treats KD as a flexible, configurable component of compression pipelines rather than a single recipe: methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, channel- or relation-level signals), how transfer is organized (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free/zero-shot), and how KD is combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, adversarial training). Empirical evidence shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the chosen distillation signals and objectives, and data availability or synthesis strategies. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable, task-aware tool integrated with other compression and robustness practices.

papers_seen.author: Gomez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses a variety of transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure, and contrastive objectives), training protocols (offline, online/co-distillation, multi‑teacher, and self‑distillation), and data strategies (real-data, synthetic or generator-based, data‑free, and federated) and is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD routinely achieves favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities when its design is matched to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. However, KD is context‑sensitive: its reliability depends on careful choices about what and how to transfer, mitigation of transferred errors and biases, and integration with complementary compression and data practices. Open challenges remain in principled transfer design, robust data‑free and privacy‑aware distillation, heterogeneous teacher–student alignment, and automating end‑to‑end compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. A rich palette of distillation targets and training regimes—soft logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free protocols—enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and communication while often preserving much of teacher performance. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable, task-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline that aligns teacher signals to student capacity, combines distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), and applies explicit mitigations for fairness, privacy, and distributional shift. The approach is powerful but context-dependent: success depends on teacher quality, student architecture and capacity, available data or synthesis mechanisms, and careful objective and curriculum design.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language modalities, KD variants (logit matching, feature/attention matching, data-free/adversarial synthesis, multi-teacher and self-distillation) enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, avoidance of bias propagation, and principled design choices for heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, configurable family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains, KD reduces latency, memory, and compute while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. KD encompasses many targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial/data‑free synthesis, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies appropriate to the task and deployment constraints. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and mitigation of failure modes such as optimization difficulties, bias transfer, and degradation on rare phenomena. Important open directions include principled objectives, robust/private distillation under data scarcity, and specialized protocols for structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Valentine
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Configurable Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When used as a configurable core of integrated compression pipelines—paired with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—KD routinely yields substantial reductions in latency, memory, and communication while preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. However, KD is not a standalone panacea: its empirical success depends on task- and data-aware choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors, bias, and distributional failures. Responsible deployment requires combining KD with complementary compression and privacy techniques and evaluating known failure modes under realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Drake
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Dependent Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile, empirically proven approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD enables substantial trade-offs among accuracy, latency, memory, and privacy when paired with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of propagated errors or bias. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Bell

Nevertheless, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data and capacity matching, and explicit mitigation of bias and distribution-shift risks, so it should be used as a configurable component within broader compression and deployment pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. A diverse toolkit — matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features and attention, many-to-many layer mappings, projector-based feature transforms, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or adversarial sample synthesis — enables large reductions in parameters and inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. papers_seen.author: Quinn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential but Not Sufficient — A Case for Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated toolkit that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. papers_seen.author: Parrish

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated set of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble ‘‘teacher’’ models into smaller, deployable ‘‘student’’ models. The technique operates at multiple levels (output distributions, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, or via synthesized data) and is commonly combined with complementary compression mechanisms (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). papers_seen.author: Gonzales

papers_seen.author: Bautista

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically grounded family of methods for producing smaller, faster, and deployment-ready models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into compact students. KD techniques include soft-label (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and adversarial- or sample-based refinements. KD interoperates with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and supports diverse protocols (offline teacher→student, multi- and ensemble teachers, online/self-distillation, data‑free and privacy-aware regimes). Practical success routinely requires task- and deployment-aware choices about transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-output degradation, and transferred biases. Key open directions include principled theory for when particular signals transfer well, robust and private distillation under limited or heterogeneous data, and reliable distillation across heterogeneous architectures and structured/generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are no longer just ways to reduce parameter counts; when designed thoughtfully they preserve or even improve task performance, domain robustness, and privacy while enabling real-time deployment. Effective distillation requires going beyond matching output probabilities: transferring internal representations, using task- and domain-aware selection of teacher signals, leveraging ensemble or adversarial schemes when appropriate, and adopting data-aware or data-free augmentation techniques. In application domains from NLP to vision, multi-modal systems, and graph learning, tailored distillation strategies yield substantial speedups and parameter reductions with minimal loss (and sometimes gains) in accuracy. This paper synthesizes evidence across diverse recent works to advocate a principled, task-centered approach to distillation and compression.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practical family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models to compact student models. A rich design space—what information to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals), how to schedule training (offline, online, progressive, or data-free), and how to combine KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—makes KD applicable across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains. Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling deployment under compute, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (or synthesis), and explicit attention to robustness, bias, and distribution shift. Best results treat KD as an adaptable toolkit that must be tailored to task, data regime, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Simmons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Versatile, but Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable paradigm for producing smaller, deployable models from larger teachers. KD provides many transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure, contrastive objectives, and synthetic/data‑free protocols) and is effective across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks when paired with task- and capacity-aware design. However, KD has predictable failure modes—propagation of teacher errors and biases, capacity and distribution mismatches, difficulty preserving low-frequency or structured behaviors, and data/privacy constraints—that limit its reliability as a sole compression method. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline that includes complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), explicit teacher–student alignment, targeted data or synthetic-data strategies, and evaluation/mitigation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Evidence and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller student models. Across vision, language, graph, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD methods vary in what they transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, attention or relational structure, contrastive signals) and how they are applied (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants). Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance and can enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous hardware; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data and augmentation strategies, and complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring capabilities of large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, or more deployable models while retaining much of their task performance. Approaches span matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mappings, attention- and projector-based transfers, data-free and zero-shot schemes, multi-teacher and online protocols, and integrations with quantization, pruning, and architecture search. Empirical work across language, vision, 3D perception, retrieval, and federated settings shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation is combined with suitable data strategies, teacher design, and complementary compression methods. Important open challenges remain in data-scarce or privacy-sensitive regimes, robust transfer across heterogeneous architectures, and principled selection of what and how to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, relational or contrastive structure, and can be arranged in offline, online, multi-teacher, or data-free regimes. When chosen and executed with attention to teacher quality, data regime, distilled signals, and student capacity, KD often recovers much of the teacher's performance and enables on-device and privacy-aware deployments. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on context and must be combined with complementary compression and training choices (e.g., architecture search, pruning, quantization, layer mapping, or domain adaptation) to meet production constraints and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD reliably improves student performance when teacher quality, student capacity, distilled signals, and data strategies are chosen with task and deployment constraints in mind. However, KD is not a universal cure: maximal, reliable gains typically arise when distillation is integrated into an overall compression pipeline that also includes pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into compact student models. The literature converges on a broad toolkit—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, ensemble and self-distillation, online/multi-teacher protocols, and data‑aware or data‑free variants—together with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis strategies, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and degraded rare-token behavior. Treating KD as a configurable, task‑aware component of an integrated compression pipeline yields the most reliable deployment outcomes.
