papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Configurable Core of Integrated Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, versatile set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across modalities. Empirical evidence shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but its reliability is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data regime, and the chosen distillation targets and protocol determine outcomes. For robust, deployment-ready compression, KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies, and fairness/privacy safeguards—rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Lester
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically important family of techniques for producing compact student models from larger teacher models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and constrained-deployment settings, KD uses diverse transfer targets and training protocols to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals, student capacity, and data strategies to task and deployment constraints and on integrating KD with complementary compression methods and privacy-aware procedures.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical approach for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants and training protocols enable large reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Real-world success depends on task- and capacity-aware choices of distillation signals, teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including data-free and federated variants), and combination with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is powerful but conditional: it frequently yields strong trade-offs in practice but requires careful treatment of teacher quality, data regimes, and robustness or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods provide practical routes to deploy high-performing deep models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints. The literature has developed diverse approaches that transfer information via soft logits, intermediate features, attentional maps, channel-wise statistics, and online mutual learning; adaptations address task-specific compression, data-free or few-shot regimes, large-scale distributed training, and teacher-student co-optimization. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, and that selecting what, when, and how to transfer knowledge (e.g., logits vs. features, offline vs. online, task-aware filtering) is crucial to achieve favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Oconnor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Foundational, Task‑Aware, and Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically indispensable family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD reduces memory and latency and can preserve much of a teacher’s performance when deployed thoughtfully. However, its reliability depends on careful, task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to select or synthesize data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques and safeguards against bias and distributional failure. I argue KD should be treated as the practical core of an integrated, task-aware compression toolkit rather than a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD methods vary by what is transferred (teacher logits, internal representations, attention, relational structure), how layers are aligned or projected, and how data constraints (limited access, privacy, or distribution shift) are handled. Empirical work demonstrates that combining output-level and representation-level objectives, using layer-mapping or projector modules, and adapting training data or curricula yields the best trade-offs between compactness and accuracy. Despite wide success, effective distillation requires careful choices about teacher quality, distilled signals, sample selection, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD reliably reduces inference cost and often preserves most of a teacher's performance, but its success depends on aligning distillation objectives, data, and teacher–student capacity with task and deployment constraints. Treating KD as a configurable element within an integrated compression pipeline—combined with representation alignment, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design—yields the most reliable and deployable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Practicalities, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving much of task performance. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple logit matching into a broad set of targets and protocols—soft targets, intermediate-feature alignment, attention/relational objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and multi- or self-distillation—frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is effective across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and alignment of data (or synthetic alternatives), and careful design of objectives and pipelines. Remaining practical limits include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, and reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints; current remedies emphasize task-aware objective design, multi-signal supervision, teacher adaptation, and integration with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of methods for producing smaller, faster, and deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into compact students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, generative, and multimodal tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and online or multi-teacher schemes—enable substantial efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance. Reliable use of KD depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability (or synthetic/data-free strategies), and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). To realize robust, real-world deployment, KD is best treated as a configurable, task-aware component within an integrated compression pipeline that includes explicit safeguards for privacy, fairness, and out-of-distribution behavior.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have been adapted across modalities (vision, language, graphs, and generative models) to produce smaller, faster, or more robust models while attempting to retain performance of larger teachers. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational information, or structural/topological properties), how transfer is scheduled or weighted (confidence-aware, progressive replacement, or multi-teacher aggregation), and how distillation is combined with other compression methods (pruning, architecture search, or compact operator substitution). Empirical work shows strong practical benefits—improved runtime, memory, and sometimes robustness or fairness—while theoretical and analytical work begins to explain when and why distillation helps (e.g., role of soft targets, label smoothing analogies, and behavior with imperfect teachers). Remaining challenges include transferring rare-word or low-frequency information in sequence tasks, preserving relational/global structure in graph and link tasks, adapting to evolving domains, and automating generator compression for GANs. This synthesis summarizes key methods, insights, and open directions from recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Luna
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, flexible approach for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational signals, or synthesized inputs to produce compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical success is highly context-dependent: it hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and complementary compression choices. Best practice treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution. Persistent challenges include reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, robust transfer of rare behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and automating teacher–student alignment for heterogeneous deployments.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression: Effective but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs, but its success is strongly context dependent. Practical deployments treat KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—rather than a standalone solution. Responsible application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and targeted mitigations for bias, rare behaviours, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Shepherd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically supported toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants (logit/soft-target matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-aware workflows) consistently enable favorable trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and model size. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, availability and match of data, and distribution shift shape outcomes. For robust, production-ready compression, KD should be configured and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design), data strategies, and task-aware safeguards against bias and low-frequency failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become primary approaches for deploying high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings. The literature spans methods that transfer soft-labels, internal feature representations, and ensemble knowledge; extensions address teacher imperfections, data scarcity or privacy, task-specific adaptations for NLP and vision, and hardware-aware compression. Empirical work demonstrates that careful design choices—such as which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student layers, whether to incorporate self-distillation or multi-teacher training, and how to combine pruning or low-precision numerics—substantially affect final accuracy and efficiency. The field also benefits from theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Remaining challenges include distilling robust semantics for low-frequency phenomena, distillation without access to original data, and co-design for hardware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Conley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically grounded technique for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs across modalities when combined with careful teacher–student design, appropriate distillation targets, and complementary compression methods. However, its strengths are conditional: practitioner success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit evaluation and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Atkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used toolkit for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into compact student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods and training protocols have diversified well beyond soft-label matching to include feature- and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, self- and online-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. KD frequently delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with architecture-aware student design and complementary compression methods, but its success is context dependent and requires deliberate handling of teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and failure modes such as bias transfer and degradation on rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically proven family of methods for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD spans output-level soft-target supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocols such as online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data-free/synthetic-data approaches. KD is most effective when embedded in an integrated, task- and hardware-aware compression pipeline that also leverages complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies. Its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals and layer mappings, and mitigation of failure modes such as propagated teacher errors, degraded long-tail behavior, distribution shift, and fairness/privacy risks. Best practice treats KD as a configurable toolkit—selected and tuned to the target task, data regime, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Avila
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Task‑Aware Toolbox — Powerful but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD reliably reduces inference cost and often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance when applied with task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data, privacy, and deployment constraints. However, KD has clear limits — capacity and architecture mismatch, data scarcity and distribution shift, and the risk of propagating teacher errors or bias — so it is best used as the configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline combined with pruning, quantization, architecture co-design, and explicit fairness/privacy safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, objective design, and architecture alignment. To realize KD's benefits in production and research, practitioners should treat distillation as a configurable component of compression pipelines—combining logits and representation matching, data-aware schedules or synthesis, and complementary compression methods—while applying targeted safeguards for robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are now essential for deploying high‑performing deep models in resource‑constrained settings across vision, speech, recommendation, graph, and language tasks. KD delivers large efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: teacher inference cost, data mismatches introduced by distillation, low‑frequency token degradation, privacy considerations, and heterogeneous deployment constraints each demand tailored remedies. Combining complementary strategies — multi‑teacher distillation, student‑aware teacher design, projector/feature adaptation, self‑distillation, exposure to raw data, and privacy-aware or federated KD — yields robust compressed models that approach or match teacher capabilities in practice.

Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and explicit handling of distribution shift, low-frequency behaviors, privacy, and architecture heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and complementary model-compression techniques constitute a practical toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. The field has expanded beyond simple logits-matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free generation, curriculum and online protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when student capacity, data availability, and teacher–student alignment are appropriately managed, but important challenges remain including handling low-frequency phenomena, teacher bias propagation, distributional mismatch, and reliable transfer under data scarcity or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used family of techniques for transferring capabilities from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce latency, memory, and energy costs while preserving task performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal domains, KD has evolved beyond logits-only supervision into rich protocols that match intermediate features, attention patterns, relational or contrastive structures, and even synthesized data or generator-based replay. Practical deployments combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies; success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and careful objective and layer alignment. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical patterns, practical recommendations, and open challenges documented in the provided literature.

papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more robust models across computer vision, NLP, multilingual metrics, and multimodal tasks. A range of complementary techniques — layer-wise mapping, data-free and zero-shot synthesis, self-distillation, adversarial and robust distillation, online/ensemble methods, and task-adaptive architecture search — together make distillation applicable under constraints such as limited data, privacy restrictions, heterogeneous devices, and production-scale training. I argue that adopting a portfolio of distillation strategies, chosen to match data availability and deployment constraints, yields the best trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, robustness, and interpretability for modern deep learning systems.

Empirical and conceptual work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, signal choice, data availability or synthesis strategy, and careful integration with other compression tools. papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure) and succeed across modalities when integrated into task‑aware compression pipelines. While KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs, reliable deployment requires explicit attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and safeguards against bias and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for compressing large or ensemble deep models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of task performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure), how distillation is arranged (offline, online, multi- or self-distillation), and how data is used or synthesized; when combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptations, KD supports deployments under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD produces strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, graphs, reinforcement learning, and generative models) but requires task-aware design—matching distilled signals to student capacity, coping with limited or mismatched data, and mitigating propagation of teacher errors—to be reliable in production.

papers_seen.author: French
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across modalities and tasks, a broad set of distillation targets and protocols—ranging from soft logits to intermediate feature and attention matching, relational or contrastive signals, and data‑free synthesis—has enabled substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving much of teacher performance. Effectiveness is context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and careful design of objectives, layer alignment, and complementary compression steps determine outcomes. Open problems include principled theory of transfer, robust transfer under distribution shift or privacy constraints, and preserving rare or structured outputs in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and often indispensable method for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance when its objectives, data strategies, and student architectures are chosen with task and deployment constraints in mind. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability, and explicit handling of transferred errors, biases, and rare-case failures. For robust, production-ready compression, KD should be applied as a configurable, task-aware element of an integrated compression pipeline that also leverages representation-aware objectives, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary architecture-aware transformations.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression That Must Be Task‑Aware and Integrated
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models from larger teachers. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and communication overhead. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core technique that is combined with task-aware design and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and that explicitly mitigates risks such as bias transfer, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Necessary but Not Sufficient Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and flexible framework for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, multimodal, and distributed settings. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what is distilled, how teacher and student are aligned, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression techniques. Practical success therefore requires integrating KD with task-aware engineering—data strategies, multi-objective compression (pruning/quantization/architecture search), teacher/student co-design, and privacy-aware protocols—to avoid known failure modes and meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible set of techniques to compress large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, language, generative modeling, and structured prediction domains, KD variants — including logit transfer, feature mimicking, self-distillation, data-free distillation, and task-specific adaptations — provide concrete trade-offs between model size, compute, and accuracy. When combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, low-precision numerics, pruning and layer skipping, or teacher training tailored to students, distillation yields practical, deployable models applicable to constrained hardware and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Empirical Findings and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD produces substantial efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance. Its success is context-dependent: it requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, what data to use (or synthesize), and how to mitigate failure modes such as bias transfer, degraded long‑tail performance, and distribution shift. Integrating KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with targeted data or optimization strategies yields the most reliable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature develops multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training protocols (offline multi-stage, online, self-distillation, data-free/generative, adversarial), and application-specific adaptations (NLP transformer compression, vision, speech, graph models, federated and privacy-aware settings). Empirical work shows KD frequently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when paired with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods, while remaining sensitive to teacher quality, data availability, and distributional or fairness concerns. Practical success generally requires matching the distillation objective to the task, handling data limitations with augmentation or synthetic generators, and integrating KD into a broader compression portfolio (pruning, quantization, architecture search).

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Component of Task‑Aware Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models, producing compact systems suitable for resource‑constrained deployment. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or hardware‑optimal compression. Reliable production compression pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable core element that must be combined with teacher–student co‑design, data strategies (including data‑free synthesis), and complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation to meet practical constraints and mitigate failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking model size and latency while preserving performance across computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation, and federated settings. Research has expanded beyond the original logits-matching paradigm into feature mimicking, many-to-many layer mapping, teacher engineering, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and task-adaptive compression. Empirical and theoretical work highlights important interactions between data complexity, teacher strength, inductive bias, and augmentation strategies, and identifies practical challenges including model-heterogeneity, data heterogeneity, and the need for robust data-free methods. The field increasingly emphasizes not only how to distill but also what to distill (logits, features, inter-class relations, view- or task-specific knowledge) and how to adapt distillation to application constraints (privacy, federated settings, domain shifts, resource budgets).

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. A broad set of objectives and protocols—logit-level supervision, feature/attention alignment, relational and contrastive signals, adversarial or synthesized-data methods, and online or multi-teacher schemes—has been developed and is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and targeted engineering (layer mapping, projectors, curriculum), and remaining challenges include teacher-bias propagation, data-domain mismatch, optimization instability, and preserving low-frequency behaviors in structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applied family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into compact students. KD routinely achieves strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities and tasks when its objectives, teacher–student design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods are chosen with deployment constraints in mind. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and distribution, and explicit safeguards against bias, robustness, and privacy failures. Best practice treats KD as a configurable building block embedded in an integrated compression pipeline tailored to the task and environment.

papers_seen.author: Hammond
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically supported family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably improves efficiency across modalities and tasks when designed as a configurable part of an integrated compression pipeline, but it is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature establishes a rich taxonomy of distillation signals (output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive objectives), training protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free and privacy-aware methods), and engineering patterns (projectors, curricula, layer mappings). Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve student generalization, but success is context dependent and benefits from integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design). Practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student capacity and alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of robustness, bias, and rare-token failures.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted framework for transferring knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models into smaller, faster, or more deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, generative modeling, and multimodal tasks, KD methods trade off accuracy, latency, and resource use by transferring different forms of information (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, or synthesized training examples). Empirical work shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve generalization and deployment feasibility, but KD has practical limits tied to teacher–student capacity mismatch, data availability, bias transfer, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena. Effective deployment mixes careful choice of distilled signals, data and augmentation strategies, multi-teacher or confidence-weighting schemes, and integration with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression, Robustness, and Privacy in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more robust models. Beyond mere size reduction, contemporary KD techniques transfer internal representations, enable deployment under data- and privacy-constrained conditions, mitigate architectural and modality mismatches, and interact non-trivially with regularization practices. I argue that KD should be treated as a foundational toolchain in applied deep learning and NLP systems—one that must be combined with tailored alignment, privacy-preserving, and teacher-selection strategies to fully realize its benefits in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When designed around task objectives, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints—and when combined with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely reduces inference cost, memory footprint, and communication overhead while preserving much of teacher performance. Yet KD is not automatic: it requires careful choices about distillation signals, architecture alignment, data strategies (including data‑free or synthetic data when originals are unavailable), and safeguards to avoid propagating teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. The literature shows a diverse set of distillation targets and training regimes, and repeatedly demonstrates that KD—when matched to task constraints and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies—can deliver large reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance. Success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, objective design, and explicit practices to mitigate propagated biases and robustness failures. Remaining open problems center on formalizing when specific KD signals preserve generalization, reliable distillation under scarce or private data, transfer across heterogeneous architectures, and principled mitigation of harmful transferred behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Context‑Sensitive, and Best Used in Hybrid Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably converts large teacher models into smaller, deployable students and is a practical cornerstone of contemporary model compression in vision, language, and multimodal systems. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student design and capacity, data availability or synthesis, and careful mitigation of failure modes such as teacher error propagation and distribution shift. For robust, real-world deployments, KD should be treated as a configurable core component within integrated compression pipelines that combine representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary methods like pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Tool for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones into a broad set of methods that address efficiency, domain adaptation, privacy, robustness, fairness, and cross-modal transfer. By moving beyond simple logits matching to layer- and feature-level alignment, multi-teacher schemes, data-free and few-shot settings, and meta-learned teachers, distillation can both preserve performance and add functional guarantees (e.g., robustness, fairness) that are crucial for real-world deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a foundational component of model compression pipelines and of strategies for adapting large pre-trained models to constrained, specialized, or sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used framework for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models while retaining much of the original performance. A diverse family of distillation objectives and workflows—ranging from soft-label/logit matching to feature- and representation-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial schemes, multi-teacher and self-supervised variants—has been developed and adapted across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs, and generative models). Empirical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on choices of distillation targets, teacher quality and friendliness, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and task-specific adaptations. Open challenges include handling mismatches in capacity or data, preserving rare-token or long-tail behavior, and formalizing best practices for combining KD with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Schneider
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller student models. Across modalities and tasks KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when combined with deployment-aware design and complementary compression methods. Its practical success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals and data strategy, and explicit measures to mitigate transferred biases, low-frequency failures, and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Conditional, and Best Used within Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable and practically effective toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD can recover much of teacher performance, enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, and be extended across logits, feature, attention, and data‑free paradigms. Its effectiveness, however, is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and selection of distillation data, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable, task‑aware component that must be combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search), data strategies, and robustness/fairness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behaviors and internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, recommendation, graph, and federated settings, KD variants—ranging from logit-based soft-label transfer to feature- and layer-level matching, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and ensemble or multi-teacher approaches—have enabled deployment on constrained devices, improved inference latency, and supported privacy- and domain-aware workflows. Practical deployment mixes KD with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-conditioning strategies; however, limitations remain around teacher–student mismatches, propagation of teacher errors and biases, data availability, and optimization stability. The literature proposes targeted remedies (attention-based layer mapping, student-friendly teacher training, few-shot and zero-shot approaches, and federated KD protocols) and points toward continued work on principled teacher design, privacy guarantees, hardware-aware objectives, and robust distillation for low-resource regimes.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while often preserving—sometimes even improving—task performance. Methods operate at the level of logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or decision boundaries and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and federated or data-free workflows. Practical deployments require careful alignment of teacher and student inputs and objectives, attention to data availability and privacy, and strategies for dealing with capacity gaps and distributional heterogeneity. Across vision, language, speech, recommender, and multimodal tasks, tailored distillation pipelines enable compact models suitable for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Moody
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Powerful, but Insufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically supported approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels (outputs, intermediate representations, relations) and has enabled substantial gains in latency, memory, and deployability across vision, language, generative, and multimodal applications. However, its success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distillation signals, and the availability or synthesis of appropriate data strongly shape outcomes. In practice KD functions best as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline that also employs pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and task- or data-aware training procedures to mitigate bias, distribution-shift, and low-frequency failures.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large models and transferring knowledge across architectures, datasets, and modalities. Research has advanced along several axes: designing distillation objectives (logit- and feature-based), aligning intermediate representations, performing distillation without access to original data, applying KD for domain adaptation and continual learning, and compressing or distilling generative and multimodal models. Practical deployments emphasize heterogeneous teacher-student settings, privacy and federated scenarios, and task-adaptive compression for resource-constrained inference. This review synthesizes the main methods, empirical findings, and practical considerations reported across recent work, and highlights open challenges and promising directions.

papers_seen.author: Pitts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. KD techniques span soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level objectives, relational/contrastive signals, and protocols such as offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, and data‑free variants. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks KD routinely reduces latency, memory, and compute while recovering much of teacher performance, but its success is context-dependent: outcomes hinge on signal choice, teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and integration with complementary compression primitives. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable core of broader compression pipelines, guided by task-aware design, teacher–student co‑engineering, and targeted mitigations for bias, robustness, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis reviews empirical and methodological advances in knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques as applied across vision, language, generative models, retrieval, recommender systems, federated and lifelong learning. It summarizes mechanisms for transferring teacher knowledge to smaller students (soft labels, intermediate representations, curriculum and selective sample strategies), practical challenges (data availability, teacher cost, domain shift, privacy, and bias), and targeted solutions (data-free distillation, fast label generation, multi-teacher and domain-adaptive schemes, self-distillation, and distillation-aware pruning). The goal is to map what the provided literature reports about when distillation helps, when it can hurt, and which strategies are effective for different settings and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and versatile approach for transferring functionality from large teacher models to compact students, enabling deployment under constraints of latency, memory, compute, and privacy. Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and optimization tasks shows KD can recover much of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization or robustness. However, KD alone is rarely sufficient for robust, production-ready compression: success depends on task-aware signal selection, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and integration with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Practical pipelines treat KD as a configurable core integrated with data and architectural strategies and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Kelly
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teachers into smaller students. When treated as a configurable core within integrated compression pipelines and paired with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, privacy-preserving protocols), KD routinely yields large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. Its success is, however, conditional: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability, and explicit mitigation of propagated biases, rare-case failures, and distribution shift determine outcomes. Best practice treats KD not as a turnkey cure but as a task‑aware, engineered component of end-to-end compression and evaluation workflows.

However, KD is not a turnkey cure: its best outcomes arise when it is treated as a configurable, context‑aware core of an integrated compression pipeline that combines distillation with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and rare‑event behavior.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD routinely produces compact models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but its success is strongly context dependent: it requires task‑aware design of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and explicit mitigations for known failure modes. The practical position argued here is that KD should be treated as the configurable, central element of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis/augmentation, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy—rather than as a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language modalities, KD variants (logit matching, feature/attention matching, data-free/adversarial synthesis, multi-teacher and self-distillation) enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, avoidance of bias propagation, and principled design choices for heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical set of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models in deep learning and NLP. Effectiveness depends on matching the distillation signals to student capacity and task structure, and on addressing failure modes such as teacher bias and data scarcity. Combining KD with complementary techniques (quantization, architecture transformations, pruning, and task-aware layer mapping) yields the best tradeoffs between compression and downstream accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.
