papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied compression techniques provide a practical toolkit for shrinking large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their task performance. Over the last decade researchers have developed a range of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational maps, contrastive signals), teacher-student schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher, lifelong), and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search, block-structured pruning). Empirical work shows KD often acts both as information transfer and regularization, enabling deployment across vision, language, multimodal, graph, generative, and medical-imaging tasks; however, success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of propagated errors or biases. Best practice is task- and capacity-aware design that combines appropriate distilled signals, alignment of inputs/representations, and complementary compression methods to meet target constraints.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely adopted approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces inference cost and often preserves much of teacher performance across modalities, but its success is context-dependent: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data and augmentation choices, and optimization design. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of a compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, data strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware adaptations—rather than a universal, standalone cure-all. I argue KD should be the default core of model-compression workflows while being explicitly adapted to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central tools for deploying high-capacity deep learning models in resource-constrained settings. Methods range from transferring soft labels to matching intermediate representations, leveraging ensembles or multiple teachers, synthesizing surrogate data for data-free distillation, and integrating distillation into federated and privacy-sensitive regimes. Empirical gains have been demonstrated across computer vision, generative modeling, graph learning, and natural language processing, while theoretical work and empirical studies highlight nuanced trade-offs related to regularization, sample selection, teacher quality, and heterogeneous/distributed data. Open challenges include robust distillation under data heterogeneity, principled teacher-student design, and compression of generative and transformer models for real-world low-latency deployment.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has grown from a simple teacher→student soft-target idea into a broad, task-aware toolbox for producing compact, faster, and more deployable models in deep learning and NLP. A diverse set of distillation targets and protocols (logits, intermediate representations, attention, relational and contrastive signals; offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants) together with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of teacher performance. Practical success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment and capacity, data strategy, and mitigation of failure modes such as transferred errors, distribution shift, rare-output degradation, and privacy constraints. Treating KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—with task-aware signal selection, layer mappings or projectors, curriculum or sample-selection strategies, and, where needed, adversarial or synthetic-data protocols—yields the most reliable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Configurable Core of Practical Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for compressing large models into compact, deployable students. KD routinely recovers much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication cost, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data strategy, and integration with complementary compression primitives. Treating KD as a configurable core element of an end‑to‑end compression pipeline — with targeted choices about what to transfer, how to map layers, how to handle scarce or private data, and how to mitigate transferred errors and biases — yields the most reliable, deployment‑ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Jenkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD supports multiple transfer targets and training protocols, is effective across modalities and tasks when designed carefully, and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. However, its empirical success is context dependent: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and domain match, and objective design, and open challenges remain around robustness, fairness, low-frequency behavior, and automated, privacy-preserving deployment pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD routinely improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when matched to student capacity, distillation signals, and data regimes; however, its success is conditional on teacher quality, student architecture and capacity, data availability, and protections for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task-aware data strategies—rather than as a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Austin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods operate over multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure) and training protocols (offline, online/self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free variants). Empirical work across vision, language, multimodal, and retrieval tasks shows KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute. Reliable application treats KD as a configurable, task‑aware component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with data strategies, architecture alignment, and complementary primitives such as pruning and quantization—and requires explicit validation for robustness, fairness, privacy, and rare‑case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques form a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models by transferring knowledge from larger or specialized models. Approaches span from simple soft-label supervision to richer transfers of internal representations, intermediate-layer mappings, attention-guided projections, adversarial feature alignment, and task- or device-aware compression. KD is used across domains—image classification, detection (2D and 3D), recommendation/CTR, language model compression, federated and heterogeneous-device learning, and reinforcement learning—and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or curriculum strategies. Recent work examines theoretical aspects (e.g., bias–variance tradeoffs and statistical interactions with data augmentation), practical design choices (teacher-student layer alignment, many-to-many mappings, ensemble teachers), and extensions that address privacy, fairness, and low-data regimes. Despite strong empirical success, open problems remain in understanding when particular KD variants best transfer generalization, how to measure and mitigate transferred biases, and how to optimally combine KD with other compression primitives for different constraints.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with task‑aware distillation objectives, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely delivers strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. However, realizing robust, fair, and reliable compressed models requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, the nature and availability of distillation data, and targeted remedies for known failure modes such as bias transfer, degradation on low‑frequency phenomena, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Configurable Core of Practical Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for compressing large models into compact, deployable students. KD routinely recovers much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication cost, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data strategy, and integration with complementary compression primitives. Treating KD as a configurable core element of an end‑to‑end compression pipeline — with targeted choices about what to transfer, how to map layers, how to handle scarce or private data, and how to mitigate transferred errors and biases — yields the most reliable, deployment‑ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger, more expensive models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature has expanded from simple logit-matching to a diverse toolbox that includes intermediate-feature matching, attention and relational objectives, self- and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware search. Empirical work shows that with task-aware objectives and careful handling of teacher-student mismatches, distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision and language tasks, though important challenges remain around data scarcity, teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, and reliably distilling structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Dalton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger or richer teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD methods (soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate feature and attention matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and architecture-aware adaptations) enable substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an overall compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task-aware data strategies—and when practitioners explicitly address common failure modes such as teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, distribution shift, and transfer of undesirable teacher traits. Remaining open areas include principled theory connecting teacher signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under heterogeneous architectures or non-iid data, and guarantees for privacy and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Toolkit for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger teachers to smaller students, but its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to train, and how to integrate complementary compression methods. When designed as part of a task-aware pipeline—with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and privacy or fairness constraints—KD yields deployable models that retain much of teacher performance; treated naively it can propagate errors and fail under data- or capacity-mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Wyatt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a mature and practical set of techniques for converting large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical evidence across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows that distillation—when applied with task awareness, appropriate choice of distilled signals, and complementary compression techniques—can recover much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, and privacy. However, its success is conditional on teacher quality, data regimes, teacher–student alignment, and explicit mitigation of biases and low‑frequency failures; therefore, distillation should be integrated into end‑to‑end compression pipelines and not treated as a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD has been adapted into many variants and protocols and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods to produce deployable models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The technique yields substantial practical gains across modalities and tasks when teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and alignment of objectives are addressed; nevertheless, KD has well-documented failure modes and open challenges that require careful engineering and further research.

papers_seen.author: Hodge
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework that compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. A rich toolkit of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure), training protocols (offline, online/mutual, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free or synthetic-data approaches) and engineering practices (layer mapping, curriculum/weighting, and integration with pruning, quantization, or architecture search) has emerged. Empirically, KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while producing substantial efficiency gains, but outcomes are context dependent: success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and careful choices about what and how to transfer. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable, task‑aware component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a single off‑the‑shelf recipe.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Context‑Dependent Path for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically powerful approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining most of the teacher performance. Its effectiveness stems from diverse ways of transferring information (logits, intermediate features, relational structure), flexible training protocols (offline, online, self-, multi-teacher), and the ability to combine with complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal remedy: success depends on signal choice, data availability and quality, teacher-student pairing, and careful integration with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and task‑aware practices.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Necessity, Limits, and a Best-Practice Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster students for deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling reduced memory, lower-latency inference, and new capabilities such as task-adaptive compression, multi-task transfer, and interpretable surrogates. At the same time, distillation is not a turnkey remedy: optimization challenges, dataset and distribution mismatches, teacher bias transfer, and design choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relational structure) strongly affect outcomes. The most reliable results come from combining KD with complementary techniques (teacher adaptation, selective or curriculum-driven sample selection, representation matching, low-precision numerics, and scaled training procedures) and from tailoring the procedure to task- and deployment-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default First‑Line but Insufficient Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, and supports a wide range of transfer targets and training paradigms. However, KD alone is not a turnkey solution: reliable deployment requires task‑aware choices about what to transfer, careful teacher–student co‑design, complementary compression primitives, data and privacy strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness, long‑tail behavior, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. Across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains, KD spans soft‑target/logit matching, intermediate‑feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocols including offline, online/self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free distillation. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs and can recover a large fraction of teacher performance when applied with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data regimes, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). However, KD’s effectiveness is context‑dependent: reliable deployment requires teacher–student co‑design, careful choice of distilled signals, appropriate data strategies, and mitigations for failure modes such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, distribution shift, and degradation on rare/low‑frequency phenomena. Important open problems include principled objectives, robust/private distillation under data scarcity, and distillation for heterogeneous or structured/generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Newton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Context‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD consistently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs when applied thoughtfully, but its benefits are conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and architecture alignment. Best practice treats KD as the central component of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and explicit mitigations for failure modes such as propagated bias, distribution shift, and degradation on low‑frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically indispensable technique for compressing and adapting large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD is highly versatile—supporting logits-, feature-, attention- and relation-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and privacy- or data-constrained workflows—but it is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, what signals are transferred, data availability and distribution, and careful training protocol design. Treating KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines and combining it with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, data augmentation, and curriculum strategies) leads to the most reliable deployment outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Buchanan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Context‑Aware, and Insufficient Alone for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically validated family of techniques that reliably improves the efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs of deep models across modalities. KD enables deployment by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller students, and it supports many training protocols and transfer targets. However, KD is not a standalone solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability or synthesis of suitable data, and careful mitigation of failure modes (distribution shift, low-frequency degradation, and bias propagation). Therefore, for robust real-world deployment KD should be treated as a configurable, task‑aware core of an integrated compression pipeline that combines complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design), teacher–student co‑design, and data strategies tailored to the application.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated toolbox for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants and protocols enable substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. In practice KD is context dependent: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and explicit mitigation of transferred biases, robustness deficits, and privacy concerns. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline that combines distillation with complementary techniques—pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—rather than as a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher performance. When treated as a task‑aware toolkit and embedded within an integrated compression pipeline (including pruning, quantization, and architecture design), KD routinely yields favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs across modalities. Realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, or relational signals), teacher–student alignment, data strategies (augmentation, data‑free synthesis, or adversarial sample use), and explicit mitigations for known failure modes such as capacity mismatch, bias transfer, and degraded treatment of rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a practical, flexible approach to compressing large neural models into resource-efficient students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. Across modalities and tasks — from language and retrieval to vision, generation, and graph learning — distillation techniques enable trade-offs between accuracy, compute, and memory that make deployment feasible on constrained hardware. However, the effectiveness of distillation depends strongly on the distillation objective, the information transferred (probabilities, internal representations, or structured signals), availability of original data, and care to avoid transferring undesirable teacher properties. When combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, architecture search, low-precision training, or curriculum strategies), distillation can yield compact models that approach or sometimes even exceed teacher performance while meeting practical latency and size constraints.

papers_seen.author: Coffey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD supports a wide range of transfer targets and training protocols and is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline. Its empirical strengths are balanced by context-sensitive failure modes—teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and the risk of propagating teacher biases—that require deliberate design choices and complementary methods.

papers_seen.author: Oneill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its success depends on teacher quality, data strategy, objective design, and integration with complementary compression methods. Treating KD as a configurable component of a task-aware compression pipeline—with explicit attention to data, robustness, and fairness—yields the most reliable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Wallace
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A rich family of distillation targets and protocols has been developed (from soft logits to feature- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants), and KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods and task-aware data and architecture strategies. Success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and augmentation, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as transferred bias, capacity mismatch, and degraded behavior on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD comprises a family of methods (logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and data- or adversarial synthesis) and operates under a range of protocols (offline teacher→student, multi-teacher, online/self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware regimes). Empirical work across modalities shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance, but reliable production-grade compression requires task- and deployment-aware choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and integration with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Luna
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, flexible approach for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational signals, or synthesized inputs to produce compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical success is highly context-dependent: it hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and match, and complementary compression choices. Best practice treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution. Persistent challenges include reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, robust transfer of rare behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and automating teacher–student alignment for heterogeneous deployments.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Settings, and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies are now widespread across computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation systems, and specialized settings (federated, few-shot, multi-modal, generative). Research has advanced along multiple axes: what to transfer (logits, features, attention, latent modules), how to shape the transfer (sample selection, adversarially-informed examples, curriculum, teacher ensembles, meta-learning), and special protocols for constrained environments (federated/black-box, few-shot, on-device inference). Empirical work shows KD can substantially close the performance gap between small and large models, enable practical deployment of generative and discriminative models, and, when extended, transfer robustness and interpretability. Remaining challenges include error propagation from teachers (especially for low-frequency phenomena), limitations under data heterogeneity in federated settings, and task-specific design choices for complex outputs (e.g., detection, segmentation, set outputs), motivating continued work on tailored distillation objectives and teacher-student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD methods include transferring soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals, and can be applied in offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data-free settings. Empirical evidence shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and enables many practical applications across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, available data (or synthesis strategies), and careful objective design. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component of broader compression pipelines—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and targeted data strategies—and adopt safeguards for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for compressing large or ensemble deep models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of task performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure), how distillation is arranged (offline, online, multi- or self-distillation), and how data is used or synthesized; when combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptations, KD supports deployments under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD produces strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, graphs, reinforcement learning, and generative models) but requires task-aware design—matching distilled signals to student capacity, coping with limited or mismatched data, and mitigating propagation of teacher errors—to be reliable in production.

papers_seen.author: Jennings
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Practical, but Not Sufficient Alone for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and empirically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD spans many transfer targets and training protocols and often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is context-dependent: its success requires careful, task-aware choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability and privacy, and how to pair distillation with complementary compression tools. Treating KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline—rather than a single recipe—yields the most reliable path to deployable, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Foundational, Context-Dependent, and Best Deployed as Part of an Integrated Compression Toolkit
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful set of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD variants—from logits and feature matching to self-, multi-teacher, and data-free protocols—have been shown to reduce model size and latency while often retaining much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, generative, and detection tasks. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, what is transferred, and interactions with other training practices. To realize KD’s practical value one should design distillation around task objectives and deployment constraints and combine it with complementary compression and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthetic Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—matching teacher logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployment commonly integrates KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires careful, task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. Key challenges include propagation of teacher errors, degradation on low-frequency or structured outputs, data and domain mismatch, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware, and Complementary Tool for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teachers into compact students. KD routinely enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, and supports a spectrum of signals and training protocols. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and distribution shift. I argue that KD should be treated as a central, configurable component of compression pipelines—powerful when combined with complementary methods and careful engineering, but requiring task‑aware safeguards to be reliable in production.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Patterns, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practically essential family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Research across vision, language, multimodal, generative, and reinforcement-learning settings has produced a toolkit of transfer targets and training protocols that, when combined with complementary compression primitives, routinely yield large reductions in latency and memory with modest performance loss. KD’s success is highly context-dependent: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and careful objective and curriculum design. Remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preservation of low-frequency behaviors, bias transfer, and privacy-aware or data-free regimes; best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all remedy.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations across modalities and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability (or synthesis), and careful choice of transfer signals; for robust, real-world compression KD should be treated as a configurable component of integrated pipelines that include complementary compression primitives and explicit safeguards for bias, robustness, and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while often preserving—sometimes even improving—task performance. Methods operate at the level of logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or decision boundaries and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and federated or data-free workflows. Practical deployments require careful alignment of teacher and student inputs and objectives, attention to data availability and privacy, and strategies for dealing with capacity gaps and distributional heterogeneity. Across vision, language, speech, recommender, and multimodal tasks, tailored distillation pipelines enable compact models suitable for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for transferring behavior and representations from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving most of a teacher's performance. Its practical value emerges when KD is used as a configurable core within integrated compression pipelines that also employ pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies. At the same time, KD is not sufficient by itself: success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distillation signals, and careful handling of data, bias, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Maxwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practical family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. Empirical results across vision, language, and speech show KD frequently recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. KD is versatile—supporting output-level, representation-level, relational, and contrastive transfer—and is most effective when treated as a configurable element within an integrated compression pipeline that also employs pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data-aware strategies. Success is conditional on task- and capacity-aware choices, availability and selection of distillation data, and explicit attention to failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, difficulty modeling low-frequency phenomena, and distribution shift.

However, KD is not a universal remedy: careful protocol design, combination with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behaviors are required for dependable real‑world deployment.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller, more deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD techniques—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or privacy-preserving protocols, and online/co-distillation schemes—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute with modest accuracy loss when applied with task-aware design. Effective use of KD typically combines careful selection of what to transfer, attention to teacher–student capacity and data regimes, and integration with complementary compression mechanisms such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. A diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals), protocols (offline/online, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, data‑free/federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) allows practitioners to recover a substantial fraction of teacher performance across modalities when teacher–student compatibility, data strategy, and optimization design are carefully managed. KD is most reliable when embedded in a task‑aware compression pipeline that attends to data availability, teacher quality, student capacity, and safeguards for robustness and fairness; persistent challenges include principled theory for diverse objectives, reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and preserving rare or structured behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Context‑Sensitive, and Best Used in Hybrid Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven technique for converting large teacher models into smaller, efficient students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD reliably reduces latency, memory, and energy costs and can transfer robustness or domain knowledge, but it is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher and student design, data regime, and deployment constraints. For robust, deployable compression, KD is best treated as a configurable core component within integrated pipelines that combine representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller student models. KD has grown from simple soft-label matching into a rich toolbox that includes intermediate feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher protocols, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve deployment trade-offs (latency, memory, privacy), but its success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment and capacity, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their capabilities. KD enables deployment across modalities and constrained environments, and empirical work shows it can approach teacher performance when combined with complementary techniques. However, KD is not a universal solution: it can propagate teacher errors and biases, struggle under data scarcity or mismatch, and require careful choices of distilled targets, architectures, and training schedules. To realize KD's benefits in production and research settings, practitioners should pair distillation with targeted remedies—representation-aware objectives, data-and-curriculum strategies, ensemble or adversarial schemes, and fairness or privacy interventions—tailored to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely used family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft logits to intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive signals—and supports varied training protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, and data‑free variants). While KD routinely delivers meaningful efficiency gains with modest performance loss, reliable deployment requires integrating distillation with task‑aware design choices, complementary compression primitives, and explicit strategies to mitigate limitations such as data scarcity, teacher bias, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Patton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation Is a Central but Insufficient Component of Model Compression: An Argument for Integrated, Task‑Aware Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely used approach for producing smaller, deployable models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or hardware‑aware compression. Practical and reliable compression requires treating KD as a configurable core element within an integrated pipeline that aligns distillation signals to student capacity, combines KD with pruning/quantization/architecture design, addresses data availability and privacy, and explicitly mitigates failure modes such as bias transfer, low‑frequency behavior loss, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework that reliably produces compact, deployable models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational objectives—have been shown across vision, language, recommendation, and generative tasks to reduce latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not a singular cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data choices, and objective design, and it can propagate biases or fail on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline, combined with architecture-aware mapping, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and targeted safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Context‑Dependent for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD provides a flexible set of transfer signals and training protocols that enable substantial efficiency gains when paired with appropriate data strategies and complementary compression primitives. However, KD is context‑dependent: its effectiveness hinges on teacher–student alignment, data regime, and targeted safeguards against bias and distributional mismatch, so it should be applied as a configurable component within broader compression and deployment pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Practicalities, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and communication while often preserving much of task performance. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple logit matching into a broad set of targets and protocols—soft targets, intermediate-feature alignment, attention/relational objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and multi- or self-distillation—frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is effective across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and alignment of data (or synthetic alternatives), and careful design of objectives and pipelines. Remaining practical limits include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, and reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints; current remedies emphasize task-aware objective design, multi-signal supervision, teacher adaptation, and integration with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is widely used to compress large neural models for deployment under resource constraints and to transfer task- and domain-specific priors across models. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal problems, distillation methods go beyond matching output probabilities: modern approaches match intermediate representations, attention patterns, contrastive structure, and task-specific signals. Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student inputs and architectures, choosing losses that capture relational or localized information, addressing dataset shifts (including low-frequency token behavior), and carefully choosing which teacher signals to transfer. Several family-specific solutions (detection, retrieval, non-autoregressive translation, graph learning, vision-language, and spoken QA) show distillation can both improve accuracy and reduce inference cost, but raise challenges around data availability, heterogeneity, and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Core for Practical Model Compression — Necessary but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically proven approach for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD enables substantial reductions in memory, latency, and energy while often preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, its effectiveness is context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and the specific distillation objectives matter greatly. Consequently, KD should be treated as a configurable core of integrated compression pipelines paired with complementary techniques and targeted safeguards to address robustness, fairness, and distributional challenges.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied set of techniques for producing compact student models from larger teacher ensembles or single models. The literature shows a rich taxonomy of distillation signals (soft logits, feature- and attention-level targets, relational/contrastive objectives), protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, self- or co-distillation), and engineering integrations (projector adapters, curriculum or confidence-weighting, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and cross-modal tasks indicates that carefully designed KD pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and mitigating failure modes such as transferred biases, degraded rare-output behavior, and capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Ponce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models across vision, language, speech, and other modalities. KD methods operate over multiple signals and protocols and are most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that also addresses data, architecture, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely used set of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure) and operate across diverse protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, and data‑free approaches). Empirical work shows KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection (or the ability to synthesize data), and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as transferred biases, degraded rare-case behavior, and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of integrated compression pipelines rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for transferring capabilities from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across architectures and modalities, KD methods reduce inference cost and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance; they are adaptable to settings with limited or no original training data and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and pretraining-aware workflows. Success in practice depends on careful choice of what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data and augmentation strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and degradation on rare phenomena. Important open directions include principled theory for diverse distillation objectives, reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and specialized protocols for structured or generative outputs.
